**Two properties found by measurement when my own assertions failed, both real:** the Gen 9 low-level bonus `(36-2L)/10` is **exactly x1.0 at level 13** — 13, 14 and 20 all give the same odds (measured 15 each, against 24 at level 10), so 13 is its NEUTRAL BOUNDARY rather than its last helpful level; and **a catch rate of 1 gives odds of exactly 0 at any HP**, by integer truncation, i.e. mathematically uncatchable with a plain ball. Both are source behaviour; both had me asserting the opposite first.

⚠️ **THE SHAKE COUNT IS EMITTED NOW, FOR M26B7.** That recon flags `catch_attempted` as "carrying no shake count" and proposes adding a presentation seam for exactly this — emitting it here means the catch ANIMATION has nothing to retrofit. 0-2 is a break-free, 3 is a capture.

**A full party REFUSES BEFORE THE ROLL** (Rob's decision, 2026-08-03), so a ball never wobbles and then loses the Pokémon anyway. That pairing is what makes deferring the PC safe rather than merely convenient. ⚠️ **A CATCH IS NOT A WIN**: `CAUGHT` is its own outcome, in neither the win nor the defeat set — conflating it with WON would pay prize money and could set a defeated-trainer flag. The capture ends the battle **through the phase machine** (the wild side has nothing able to act) rather than via a new "battle over" flag, which is how source gets there too.

**H5 — fleeing**, from `TryRunFromBattle` (`battle_util.c:540`). ⚠️ **EQUAL SPEED SUCCEEDS** — the roll is gated on `speed < opponent`, so a naive `>` would make same-speed encounters roll for nothing. Slower rolls `(own*128)/theirs + run_tries*30` against 0-255, with `run_tries` accumulating so a slow Pokémon is never trapped indefinitely. Ghost-types always escape (`B_GHOSTS_ESCAPE >= GEN_6`, the same rule that already exempts them from trapping).

⚠️ **`[M25b]`'S RUN PLACEHOLDER COULD NOT SIMPLY BE REPOINTED, exactly as flagged when H5 was scoped**: one button serves both battle kinds, and running from a TRAINER is a forfeit that whites the player out while running from a wild Pokémon costs nothing. The wild branch is separate; the simulator's own scene-swap Run is untouched.

**Smoke Ball gets its first purpose.** `[M24b]` shipped it data-only with a note that no flee mechanic existed to consume it; this is that mechanic. ⚠️ **Run Away is the mirror case and is NOT implemented** — `[M17n-1]` gave it no constant at all on the grounds that it is "out of battle-engine scope", which was true then and is no longer: its real effect is guaranteed escape. Flagged, not fixed — an ability-roster decision like Stench's.

⚠️ **ONE DISCLOSED GAP: A FAILED ESCAPE DOES NOT SPEND THE TURN.** Source does. This project has no "do nothing" action to queue, so the player simply picks again — which makes fleeing free, only slower. Closing it needs a real skip-turn action in the TURN MACHINE, not in the escape code, which is why it is recorded rather than bodged.

**Tests**: new `m27h_catching_test` **49/49**, stable across 3 runs (⚠️ F.05/F.06 first used a 5-vs-200 speed ratio giving a 3/256 chance, where 0 successes in 200 trials is ~10% likely and the assertion genuinely flaked; 50-vs-100 discriminates in both directions). ⚠️ **`m22_item_action_test` needed real repair, not just an arity bump**: the widened signal broke its lambda (taking four assertions down with it via the aborted function), and its own `_test_poke_ball_always_fails_regardless_of_target_state` asserted "the catch always fails (M22 stub)" and "the target is completely untouched" — both true of the stub, both now false. Rewritten to guard the new properties; **67/67**. Regression: `m27h_wild_encounters_test` 49/49, `m27a_step_resolver_test` 514/514, `m27o_field_poison_test` 57/57, `m27f_stage4_test` 63/63, `m27i_i4_bag_screen_test` 48/48, `item_test` 77/77, `m24b_test` 61/61, `switch_test` 64/64, `item_registry_test` 309/309.

**M27H IS CLOSED** — H1 through H5. ⚠️ **NOT screenshot-verified**: the formula and the round trip are driven by tests and the H1-H3 live drive, but a catch has not been watched on screen. It would show nothing anyway until **M26B7** builds the animation.

## M27M — Map authoring tooling *(new block, scoped and approved 2026-07-30)*

**[M27M-T — trimmed TileSet] SCOPED 2026-07-30, not built. ⚠️ Scope of record is `docs/m27m_trimmed_tileset_recon.md`.** Measured rather than estimated: a real trimmed twin of the Pallet Town pair loads in **1.71 ms against the full set's 15.25 ms — 8.9x**, 25 KB → 6 KB. Region-wide only **11,036 tile definitions are actually placed** against the 132,480 `create_tile()` calls made today (**4.0x**), and all fourteen corridor pairs together would build in **~31 ms** — about what ONE cold tileset costs now. Baked scenes need no re-bake (M27M2 made the TileSet an `ext_resource`), `check_bake_diff` and the overlay are unaffected, and no consumer iterates tiles. **The failure mode is SILENT and is the whole design constraint**: `set_cell` accepts a coord whose tile was never created, stores it faithfully, and renders nothing — so the trim pass must ship with its own coverage proof, not after. Three hazards are recorded there with measurements: the trim set must be computed region-wide per pair rather than per-bake (or a later map silently renders with holes), it must union `border[]` as well as `metatile[]` (**5 border ids region-wide appear in no map body**), and it conflicts head-on with M27M's authoring requirement — resolved by treating `trim`/`expand` as two idempotent operations on ONE artifact rather than shipping two files.

**A thirteenth M27 block, orthogonal to C's stitching work.** Added because this is Kanto with an ORIGINAL story: the region's 421 maps are imported, but new maps and new art are inevitable, and **there is currently no way to create either.** Scope of record while this is unbuilt: the approved mockup at `https://claude.ai/code/artifact/0cc55049-a0d4-4675-8b0c-eb33853611b0`. Nothing here is implemented.

**The architectural decision this rests on, Rob's call: THE SCENE BECOMES THE SOURCE OF TRUTH.** Import Kanto once, then hand the artifacts over to authoring rather than keeping a re-runnable pipeline. That retires machinery deliberately rather than by neglect — the baker's `_scene_divergence` guard and `check_bake_diff` both answer *"does this scene still contain only what the baker would produce?"*, and once maps carry hand-painted art **every map is non-reproducible by design**, so both become permanent false positives (the same failure fixed this session, but semantic and unfixable). `provenance` loses its guard role for the same reason. **`attr_explicit` matters MORE, not less** — it marks cells whose collision/elevation is an inherited guess, which is exactly what every newly painted cell is. Keep both guards until the Kanto import is declared done, then retire them on purpose. Accepted cost: a bug found later has no bulk-fix path except a script that rewrites `.tres` files directly.

**Painting already works and needs nothing built** — `_build_tileset` calls `create_tile` for EVERY tile in the atlas, not just used ones, so Godot's own tilemap editor can paint any metatile in a pair today. What is missing is everything downstream of the paint.

**Three findings that shaped the design.** (1) **A `behavior` custom data layer is already declared on every baked TileSet and never populated** — nothing writes it, nothing reads it; someone scaffolded this exact seam and stopped. So per-metatile attributes belong ON THE TILE via Godot's own custom data, not in a parallel resource keyed by id. (2) **Custom art needs almost no new convention**: reference metatile ids are bounded by the GBA's 10-bit mask (the corridor genuinely reaches 1023) while `MapData.metatile` is `PackedInt32Array`, so custom metatiles take ids ≥ 1024 as extra rows on the same per-pair atlas — `id % 32, id / 32` still resolves and `source_id == plane` is untouched. All 33 atlases are 0.9 MB, so headroom is not a concern. (3) **The two-plane paint is the trap.** A metatile routes to one or two of three planes, so painting a `NORMAL` one into Ground alone renders NOTHING — the identical bug that made half the C3 skirt invisible, waiting for the first person to hand-paint.

**Sub-tiers, in dependency order.** **M27M1 — populate the tile's custom data** (behaviour + layer type at bake time; finishes the half-built seam). **M27M2 — shared per-pair `TileSet` `.tres`**, replacing the copy currently embedded as a SubResource in each scene: 60 shared resources instead of 421, and adding art then updates one file rather than every consumer. **M27M3 — authoring layer + plane routing**: paint into one layer, a `@tool` distributes to the correct planes using the layer type now on the tile. **M27M4 — change detection into the review backlog**: compare painted ids against `MapData.metatile` — which earns its place NOT as a cache of the scene but as the record of what the collision and elevation were last authored AGAINST — then seed via the existing `author_cell_with_defaults()` and clear the explicit bits so the cell surfaces in `review_cells()`. Without it, painting a wall over a path leaves the cell walkable AND still marked confirmed. **M27M5 — new maps from Kanto art**: blank `.tscn` + `.tres` written straight to `scenes/maps/`, no importer and no JSON (`assets/maps/` is gitignored as regenerable output, so authored input cannot live there; §1.9's re-import policy already says *"authored maps simply are not in that set"*). **M27M6 — behaviour picker**, Rob's explicit request: a named dropdown instead of raw ints, because behaviour is a 240-value enum and Godot's custom data layers are plain typed ints with no enum hint — `metatile_behavior.gd` already carries `NAME_BY_ID` generated from source, which is exactly the table it needs. **M27M7 — new art**: 16x16 metatiles authored directly (NOT the GBA tiles+metatiles.bin encoding, which exists for hardware constraints that do not apply), appended past id 1023, each tagged once via M27M6.

**What stays a human's job, and why it is irreducible.** Measured across all 421 maps / 230,619 cells: behaviour and layer type vary by placement **0%** — per-metatile by construction, so a painted tile carries them. Collision varies **52.0%** and elevation **52.1%**, so they are properties of the POSITION and cannot be derived from the tile at all. That split is the whole design: tags travel with the tile, collision and elevation get a guess plus a review flag. **New art is the one exception** — a brand-new metatile has no behaviour or layer type anywhere, so both are authored ONCE PER TILE at ingestion, not per placement. Layer type is not derivable even in principle: whether the player walks in front of a tile or behind it is a decision.

**Two questions deliberately left open.** Whether painting directly into `Ground` should be blocked or silently routed; and whether an explicit skirt opt-out flag is worth having (see C3's note — the current empty-`border` mechanism works but cannot distinguish "deliberately none" from "lost its border").

**M27M2 SHIPPED EARLY, 2026-07-30 — it turned out to be the fix for C4's crossing stutter.** Each baked scene embedded its own `TileSet` as a `SubResource`, and building one is **2208 `create_tile()` calls** — a flat ~27 ms per scene load regardless of map size. `map_baker` now writes one shared `TileSet` per tileset PAIR to `assets/map_tilesets/` and references it as an `ext_resource`: **4 files cover the 8-map corridor, 60 would cover all 421**, replacing 421 embedded copies. `take_over_path()` after the save is load-bearing — without it the instance handed to the layers carries no `resource_path` and `ResourceSaver` writes it straight back into the scene as a `SubResource`, sharing nothing. Its original purpose is unchanged: adding custom art now updates one file per pair instead of every consumer.

**Freeze and undo — BOTH FIXED, and they were ONE defect, not two.** Rob's hands-on pass reported Ctrl+Z doing nothing and a ~5 s editor stall per collision paint. **Measured before deciding anything**: raw `ResourceSaver.save()` on the real artifacts costs **0.17 / 0.44 / 0.83 ms** for 480 / 1680 / 3726 cells — the stall was **~5000× the write**, so the write itself was never the cost; `snapshot_cells()` is ~0.001 ms and never a factor; no memory pressure (11 GiB free, 0 B swap), closing the WSLg branch. The cost was editor-side work triggered BY the write (`EditorFileSystem` rescan across 30,741 watched files, 21,979 of them `.import` sidecars). `EditorFileSystem.update_file()` was tried as the surgical fix and **did not suppress it**. **Resolved by taking the write off the paint path entirely** — and the undo defect dissolved with it: a working Ctrl+Z had been stalling exactly as long as a paint, so it read as "nothing happened". Verified live: `pre_drag=4 post=4`, one `map_data` id throughout, `restore_cells` firing on `Scene Undo`. **Both defects confirmed fixed by Rob's own hands-on pass, 2026-07-29: no lag, and Ctrl+Z reverting correctly.** That confirmation matters more than usual here — the plugin is this project's one surface with no automated coverage, so an editor-only behaviour has no other way to be checked.

**The save affordance and the dirty indicator ship in the SAME change, because either alone is a trap.** `paint()` sets `_unsaved_edits`; a loud `UNSAVED EDITS — use Save Map Data in the 2D toolbar` banner draws only while dirty; the plugin owns a **Save Map Data** button in `CONTAINER_CANVAS_EDITOR_MENU` — deliberately its own control rather than leaning on Ctrl+S, since the normal scene-save path is exactly what once put a `MapOverlay` node into a baked map and made Section N necessary. `restore_cells()` now dirties rather than saves: an undo moves memory AWAY from disk just as a paint does, so the indicator must come ON. **Deliberately NOT debounced** — a stall that fires whenever you pause to think is worse than one you can predict. One predictable stall on the button is the whole bargain.

⚠️ **A paint that changed no VALUE still changed PROVENANCE — fixed.** `set_collision`/`set_elevation` write a value, an explicit bit AND provenance, but `apply_edit`'s `changed` predicate only asked about the first two — so repainting a value that was already correct reported "nothing happened": no dirty flag, no undo entry, and a mutation that still reached disk on the next deliberate save. **Measured on a real editing pass: 8 of 38 authored cells arrived that way.** Silent was the problem, not the flip — an IMPORTED cell going AUTHORED is what makes the baker refuse a re-bake, so a gesture that changed nothing visible could quietly make a map un-re-bakeable. New `MapData.is_authored()` is the third clause, deliberately WIDER than `needs_review` (which now routes through it, so the provenance read lives in one place). `snapshot_cells()` had ALWAYS captured provenance — its own comment says a paint changes "a VALUE and an EXPLICIT BIT and possibly PROVENANCE" — so undo needed no change at all once the predicate was honest.

**Pallet Town reset to square 1.** Rob's editing pass was deliberately throwaway, so it was force-rebaked away (`map_baker.tscn -- PalletTown_Frlg --force`): 38 AUTHORED → 0, 5 review cells → 0, and the regenerated `.tres` came back **byte-identical to HEAD** and dropped out of `git status`, which also proves the baker is deterministic for that map. `--force` skips the divergence guard, so no scratch save ran and no new `SubResource` drift was introduced — `check_bake_diff --all` still reports 1 of 8, still `Route1_Frlg`.

✅ **The temporary diagnostics are GONE and painting persists again.** [This bullet previously read "TEMPORARY DIAGNOSTICS IN THE TREE — and they make painting non-persistent", warning that `save_map_data()` was commented out inside `restore_cells()`, that this was the only save call site, and that nothing worth keeping should be painted until a fix landed. All of that is now false and is corrected rather than left to alarm the next session.] Both `===== TEMPORARY DIAGNOSTIC (M27B step 1) =====` blocks are removed, `_pre_drag` is gone from the plugin, and persistence is the **Save Map Data** button's job with the dirty banner saying when it is owed — see the two paragraphs above. Verified by grep: zero diagnostic blocks anywhere in `scripts/overworld/`, `addons/map_overlay_editor/` or `scenes/overworld/`.

🔶 **KNOWN DEFECT — click-to-select disables itself.** Clicking a marker selects the entity, which makes the plugin stop handling the edited object, so `next_in_stack`'s cycling is **unreachable through the UI**. One-line fix: `EditorInterface.inspect_object()` instead of mutating the selection. **The plugin is this project's one surface with no automated coverage, and this is the third defect to ship there** after the editor clip-rect bug and whatever the undo pass finds — which is why the cycle DECISION lives on the overlay as a pure function (`next_in_stack`) and the plugin retains only the act of selecting.

**Tests.** `m27a_step_resolver_test` **44 → 295/295** via `scripts/run_overworld_tests.sh` (which fails a run on engine ERROR lines); `EXPECTED_TOTAL` **190 → 294**, gated **90 → 104**, all re-measured from real runs per the MEASURED-CONSTANT RULE. New sections: **S** (map table, entity source, warp states), **T** (sight-line maths, all five no-ray states), **U** (click hit-test), **V** (stacks, cycle, counts — using the REAL corridor overlaps as fixtures), **W** (the baker guard's normalisation, driven against scratch strings, including a repointed `[ext_resource] path=` that over-broad normalisation would mask), **X** (the paint-gesture lifecycle plus the dirty invariant — X.18-X.24 pin the provenance-only repaint above, and that fixture has to stamp BOTH explicit bits like real imported data, because `_synth`'s empty `attr_explicit` would let the pre-existing not-explicit clause catch it by accident and the test would prove nothing). Fresh-checkout path verified balancing with both `.tscn` and `.tres` moved aside.

⚠️ **Section J no longer asserts against a live editing target.** J.04-J.06 read cell (0,0) and J.07 demanded an empty review backlog — both true only while nobody had used the tool, so one saved AUTHOR-mode paint turned the suite red for doing the intended thing, and the failure read like an importer regression. J.04-J.06 now probe the first genuinely imported cell (gating cleanly if none remains); **J.07 asserts the invariant that actually holds — the importer emits no half-decided cells** — by checking every untouched cell is explicit on both attributes, which is strictly stronger than an empty-backlog check for the imported subset AND survives any amount of painting; J.10 measures a DELTA against whatever the last save left. Confirmed before relying on it that `review_cells()` is a fresh row-major rescan returning a NEW array per call, so the baseline is a real snapshot and not a view the second call mutates underneath — that, rather than ordering, was the failure mode worth checking. Riders also landed: section H now gates on both artifacts rather than gating on the `.tres` while asserting on the `.tscn`, and H.13's comment no longer claims Pallet Town carries a hand-instanced `MapOverlay` — Section N asserts that no baked map does.

## M27N — Field weather *(new block, scoped 2026-07-31)*

**Scoped, not built.** Overworld weather, which no earlier M27 scoping pass named. Distinct from battle weather (`[M26B4]`), which is a separate system — source tears field weather down at battle entry (`Transition_StartIntro`), and `battle_bg.c` has zero weather references.

**Kanto uses 4 of the 24 weather constants, and the distribution is the scoping fact.** Measured across all 419 Kanto maps: `WEATHER_NONE` 331, `WEATHER_SUNNY` 62, `WEATHER_FOG_HORIZONTAL` 19, `WEATHER_SHADE` 7. No rain, sandstorm, snow, thunderstorm, ash, drought or cycles anywhere in the region. The 32-map corridor is **7 SUNNY** (every outdoor route/town), **1 SHADE** (Viridian Forest), 24 NONE (every interior).

⚠️ **There are ZERO weather coord events in Kanto.** Weather is a per-map-header field applied on map entry, full stop — `DoCoordEventWeather` has no Kanto consumer. Recorded because a scriptless coord event is the obvious place to look for weather and finding none there could easily read as an importer gap rather than as absence. **The importer currently captures the header's `weather` field not at all.**

**SUNNY and SHADE are PURE COLOUR GRADES — no sprites, no particles, no layers.** Both have an empty `_Main`, create nothing, and set only `targetColorMapIndex` (0 for Sunny, 3 for Shade) with `colorMapStepDelay = 20`, i.e. a gradual fade between indices rather than a snap (`field_weather_effect.c:156, 2256`). The mechanism beneath is a **19 x 32 per-channel lookup table** (`sDarkenedContrastColorMaps`, plus a sibling `sContrastColorMaps`, `field_weather.c:65/88`) remapping every 5-bit palette channel, applied across all 32 palettes via `ApplyColorMap(0, 32, index)`. **FOG_HORIZONTAL is the one Kanto type that is more than a grade** — same colour map plus a scrolling fog sprite layer with its own blend coefficients (`:1372`).

**Proposed sub-tiers.** **W1** — the importer captures `weather` into `MapData` (one field; `.tres`-only, so no `--force` re-bake, per C1's precedent). **W2** — port both 19x32 LUTs verbatim plus a LUT shader on a `CanvasLayer` above the world and below the message box; verbatim tables are standing practice here (`gSineTable`'s 320 entries, `EXP_SCALING_FACTORS`' 211). **W3** — apply on map entry with the real 20-frame-per-step fade, settling during the existing warp fade. **W4, DEFERRED** — FOG_HORIZONTAL's scrolling layer; **zero corridor consumers**, so it waits for the full-region import.

⚠️ **HONEST SIZING: the corridor's entire visible payoff is one map.** Colour map index 0 is very nearly the identity (`{0,0,1,2,3...29}` — it only compresses the top end), so SUNNY on those 7 maps is close to a no-op; the real delta is Viridian Forest looking darker, shade cutting brights ~19% against sunny's ~6%. Weather becomes genuinely worthwhile at full-region import (19 fog maps, 7 shade). **It is cheap, self-contained, blocks nothing, and can drop in at any pause** — it is not a prerequisite for anything.

**Three things to settle at build time rather than guess now**: which of the two 19x32 tables is selected and by what; faithful LUT shader versus a cheap `CanvasModulate` tint (recommend the LUT — similar cost, cannot drift from source); and whether overworld weather feeds battle weather, since `field_weather` IS referenced from `battle_main.c` and `battle_util.c` but that link was NOT traced and must not be assumed either way.

## M27O — Whiteout & respawn *(new block, scoped 2026-07-31)*

**Scoped, not built.** Sequenced at the end of M27 at Rob's direction. Today, losing a trainer battle leaves that trainer beatable again and the player standing where they fell — `[M27F Stages 1 & 2]` flagged this as "the loss path is unit-tested but not live-driven, and whiteout is not modelled", and it is the one remaining correctness gap on the corridor's own critical path.

⚠️ **THERE ARE TWO TRIGGERS, NOT ONE, AND THE SECOND IS THE ONE THAT GETS FORGOTTEN.** Battle loss reaches `CB2_WhiteOut` from **seven** call sites in `battle_setup.c` (`:662, :682, :698, :1455, :1477, :1484, :1507` — the split is trainer vs wild vs scripted). But `TryFieldPoisonWhiteOut` (`field_poison.c:119`) is a wholly separate path: a party wiped by **poison damage while walking** whites out in the overworld with no battle involved at all. That half needs a field step-counter and a poison tick, neither of which exists — so it is a real sub-item to scope, not a free rider on the battle path.

**The respawn point is a saved warp, not a map id.** `lastHealLocation` is a `struct WarpData` in SaveBlock1 (`global.h:1100`, whose own comment reads *"used by white-out and teleport"*), set via `SetLastHealLocationWarp` and consumed by `SetWarpDestinationToLastHealLocation` (`overworld.h:108-118`). **This project already imports the opcode that sets it** — `setrespawn` is **47 uses** in the corpus — and `[M27C C5]`'s warp dispatch is the machinery that would consume it, so the mechanism is mostly already sitting there unwired.

**Money loss is real, formula-exact, and partly blocked here.** `sWhiteOutBadgeMoney[9] = { 8, 16, 24, 36, 48, 64, 80, 100, 120 }` (`battle_script_commands.c:315`), and the amount is `table[badge_count] * highest_party_level` **clamped to what the player actually has** (`:5887` — `if (!IsEnoughMoney(...)) money = GetMoney(...)`). Badge counting is available today (`FlagStore` from `[M27D D4]`, and Brock's own script really does set `FLAG_BADGE01_GET`), but **there is no persistent wallet** — `[M24b]` built the battle-side `money_awarded` payout with nothing durable behind it. So the formula can be ported now and the deduction cannot land until M27I/M27L give money somewhere to live.

**Two source details worth not rediscovering.** `IsLastHealLocationPlayerHouse()` (`heal_location.h:16`) is a real special case — the game distinguishes waking up at home from waking up at a Pokécentre, and the corridor's own first respawn point IS the player's house. And `BS_JumpIfNoWhiteOut` (`battle_script_commands.c:12351`) is a battle-script-level branch, meaning some scripted battles deliberately do NOT white out on a loss — a rival fight you are meant to lose must not be routed through this.

**Already declined, do not re-open**: `B_FLAG_NO_WHITEOUT` is one of the eight alternate-mode flags **M35** already owns for the simulator side; it is not an RPG-side toggle.

**Proposed sub-tiers.** **O1** — the respawn point: `setrespawn` wired into `FlagStore`-adjacent session state, defaulting to the player's house, consumed through C5's existing warp dispatch. **O2** — the battle-loss path: fade, party fully healed, warp to the saved point, and the beaten-trainer flag correctly NOT set. **O3** — money loss, once a wallet exists (blocked on M27I/M27L). **O4, DEFERRED** — the field-poison path, which needs the step-counter/poison-tick system first.

**Honest sizing**: O1+O2 are small and close the correctness gap on their own; O3 and O4 are each gated on systems that do not exist yet. Do not treat this block as one unit.


**M27C — Connected world**: stitching, border skirt, connections, warps, FRLG map-preview screen, escalators. **M27D — Entities & NPCs**: object events, movement types, trainer sight (one-tile line, object-ID order); no live-world persistence. **Detail doc: `design-object-events.md` (reviewed 2026-07-28, `docs/overworld_scope.md` §32 — sound and feasible, with two changes).** One `@tool` base scene per event category over a shared `OverworldEntity` (NPC / TrainerNPC / ItemBall / Warp / Trigger / Sign), mapping onto source's four arrays: `object_events` → NPC/TrainerNPC/ItemBall (discriminated by `graphics_id` + `trainer_type`), `warp_events` → Warp, `coord_events` → Trigger, `bg_events` → Sign. Placed instances are the single source of truth for spawn data; identity/party/class stay in `TrainerRegistry` referenced by **`trainer_key` string, NOT `trainer_id` int** (the int is a sorted-alphabetical index that shifts on regen — see M24a). **CORRECTION to the design doc**: the overworld sprite is PLACEMENT data (`graphics_id` on the object event), NOT trainer data — `TrainerData` has `trainer_pic_id` (the battle front pic) and no overworld sprite field at all, so `TrainerNPC` must not pull it from the registry. **REFRAME**: the doc reads authoring-first, but 421 maps already carry their events — the importer emits these nodes (M27B) and the editor edits them, matching the import-first-then-tweak decision. **Prerequisite**: `TrainerRegistry` needs `@tool` plus a public `all_keys()`; it is currently plain `RefCounted` with a private key index, and the editor dropdown/warnings are dead without both. **Sequencing note**: the design doc's own step 3 (`interact_script` routing) points into the field script engine (M27G) and can only be a stub until then — do the trainer path first, since it routes to an already-built battle seam. **M27E — Field moves & traversal** (absorbs the retired M32): surf/dive/waterfall, cut/strength/rock smash/flash, forced movement, fishing. **M27F — Dialogue & interaction**: interaction, the message box, and the field script VM. **Two corrections to this line's own original wording, both from the built result** (2026-07-31): the **Dialogue Manager plugin is NOT used** — its typewriter was vendored into `scripts/overworld/text_typer.gd` rather than duck-typing into `DialogueLabel`'s private seam, and the plugin now has zero live consumers; and the **field script engine moved here from M27G**, built in stages against the corridor (Stage 1 interaction/dialogue, Stage 2 the battle seam, Stage 3+ movement) rather than waiting on a single large block. **M27G keeps the specials-scoping session**, which is still genuinely its own job: `special` is 1,390 uses standing for a few hundred distinct named C functions. **M27G — Field script engine**: its own block, after a dedicated specials-scoping session; realistically 30–40% of the milestone. **M27H — Encounters & battle glue**: encounter TRIGGERING (M29 owns the content/mechanics), imported Kanto tables, the battle-return results object, transitions incl. Nothing is deferred for an unread step function — building that surface would clear all of them at once.** Iconic Gen 1-3 closed at 70/70; Tier 2 (remaining Gen 1-3) and Tier 3 (Gen 4+) both past 50%. **Sub-tiers** — A Extraction ✅ · B Runtime core ✅ · C Core behavior batch ✅ · D Batched expansion 🔶 ONGOING (39 batches + deferral clearance; the per-scanline surface was built in batch 37) · E Backgrounds & screen effects ✅ (E1/E2/E3) · **S SFX & audio surface — NOT STARTED** (owns its own recon of the project's entire missing audio surface; the project ships no audio at all) · **H Hand-authored animations — RESEARCHED, NOT STARTED** (escape hatch for moves whose port reads badly; diverges from the 1x fidelity bar by design, so it is a recorded exception rather than a drift). **Where to look in `docs/m26_f1_recon.md`:** §5 proposal and §7 decisions · one section per sub-tier and per M36D batch · **`M36 — open look-calls and capability gaps`** (three appearance judgements awaiting Rob, plus the one capability gap) · **`M36 — running lists`** (upstream bugs reproduced deliberately · deferred behaviors and why · disclosed divergences — each a lookup that previously existed only inside batch prose) · `M36D batch ordering` (Decision 5's phase order amended by Rob to yield-ordering, 2026-07-30). **Standing rules for this milestone**, kept here because they govern how the next batch is run rather than recording what a past one did: (1) **Judge a batch by the shared machinery it retires, not the move count** — a behavior only completes a move if it was that move's LAST blocker, so the greedy ranking measures reach, not yield. (2) **Read each target move's ACTUAL missing set** before selecting; inferring from family names produced batch 5's recorded miss. (3) **Ask at Step 0 which candidates mutate a BATTLER** — visibility, displacement, scale/rotation or blend. That is the leak class this port has hit five times, and the VM's four restore nets exist because of it. (4) **Defer rather than guess** when a step function has not been read in full; batch 10 deferred five and batch 11 ported four of them correctly as a result. (5) **Do not "fix" a reproduced upstream bug or a disclosed divergence** without checking the running lists first. (6) **"grep found nothing" is a statement about the PATTERN, not the source.** Batch 19 added a second dress: **a missing OUTPUT file is not an absent INPUT** — three backgrounds were recorded across two batches as "never pulled" when the generator was refusing them and saying so on every run. Run the tool before describing why its output is missing. Three of batch 15's four deferrals were search failures (`static void` vs `void`; `struct Sprite*` vs `struct Sprite *`), not hard code. Defer for an unread step function, never for an unsuccessful search — they produce the same empty terminal. (7) **An assertion that cannot fail is indistinguishable from one that passes.** A spawning test guarding on `if node != null:` can skip silently — batch 13 found EIGHT wrong template names hiding 26 never-run assertions this way. Resolve template names by CALLBACK from `templates.json`, never by guessing, and keep `_test_every_template_name_resolves` green. **Batches 23 and 24 both shipped a vacuous guard that only the INJECTION caught, and the lesson behind them is the one to watch: a guard whose injection you had to hand-pick is a guard you have not tested.** Batch 23's lattice check asserted only "starts above the screen" (true of any downward march) and its zigzag check read the column-to-column jump as a sweep (so a bolt with no alternation reported one). Batch 24's phase check compared two sprites of DIFFERENT AGES, which deviate differently whether or not the mechanism under test exists at all. Injecting the plausible misreading is not a formality after the tests pass — it is the only thing separating a guard from a decoration; when the first injection passes, suspect the assertion before crediting the code. **THE PREVENTIVE FORM, which is what actually works: derive each assertion from the NEGATION, not from the truth.** The habit that produces weak guards is writing "what does the correct version do?" and asserting that. Ask instead "what would the specific plausible WRONG version do differently?" and assert the difference — ideally by writing the injection BEFORE the assertion. Every rule-(7)/(13) instance recorded here would have been caught at authoring time by that one change, without needing to be rediscovered per batch. (10) **A `Sin()` in a step function does not mean the sprite waves — the ARGS decide.** Batch 27's Sucker Punch test asserted a vertical wave reasoned from the sine call, and failed: both real call sites pass amplitude ZERO, so the term is inert wherever it is actually reached. Port the term, but check what the scripts feed it before describing the motion — the same discipline as rule (2). (11) **Upstream duplicates functions rather than calling them; check before porting.** Seven batches have turned up four verbatim groups (`AnimGunkShotParticles`≡`AnimToTargetInSinWave`, `AnimGrassKnot`≡`AnimSuckerPunch`, and `AnimForcePalm`≡`AnimPunishment`≡`AnimGunkShotImpact` — three names, one implementation), identical line for line. Register an alias and assert the identity, so a later session cannot quietly produce a second implementation to keep in step. (13) **A fixture where two competing rules AGREE cannot tell them apart.** Batch 31's Helping Hand guard used a stage where the partner rule and the side rule both give the same answer, so deleting the partner rule passed; batch 32's Dragon Rush guard asserted only that two sides DIFFER, which is true whichever battler you key on, because attacker and target are always opposite in singles. When a claim is "keyed on X, not Y", build the fixture where X and Y disagree — or pin the direction absolutely against source. Batch 38's "it moved horizontally" (true at any fixed-point scale) and batch 39's "it accelerates" (true of constant gravity as well as quadratic) are the same shape and were each caught only by injection — see rule (7)'s preventive form. Batch 39's took TWO rewrites to find an assertion that discriminates at all, which is the cost of writing the guard before knowing what it must exclude. (15) **A fixture that cannot express a claim's NEGATION must say so at the assertion.** Odor Sleuth's clones mirror because their phases start 180 degrees apart, not because the phases step opposite ways — only x is drawn, and `cos(t+128) == -cos(t)` either way, so the step directions are invisible here (b34). Zen Headbutt's "not side-mirrored" claim is invisible for a fixture reason instead: `FakeStage.facing_sign()` is a fixed 1.0 (b35). **Distinct from (7) and (13)** — there the assertion was weak and could be strengthened; here the claim is true, load-bearing and untestable. Pin what IS observable and state at the assertion that the rest rests on the source read alone, so a green test never implies coverage it lacks. (14) **Sample points matter as much as assertions.** Batch 32's spin check sampled at the sine's minimum, where stepping either direction moves Y identically, and reported a correct mirror as a failure-free match. Check what the maths is doing at the frame you chose. (12) **Which ARG REGISTER a query task answers on is per-task, not a convention.** Batch 30 found `AnimTask_IsTargetPartner` and `AnimTask_GetLycanrocForm` writing arg 0 while every neighbour writes arg 7 — correct in both cases, because those two are read by a `jumpargeq 0` on the very next line and `jumpargeq` does not reload the registers. Normalising either direction breaks real consumers. Read the call site, not the family. (9) **A comment saying "nothing consumes this" is a claim with an expiry date.** Batch 24 found `AnimTask_StartSinAnimTimer` registered as a literal no-op because, when ported, nothing read the phase register it drives — true then, false the moment `_to_target_in_sin_wave` landed, and Flamethrower had been rendering a lockstep flame stream ever since. The same batch found the VM's `_load_args` clearing all eight arg registers, which reads as hygiene and silently severs source's one cross-command channel (`gBattleAnimArgs` is a persistent global; `Cmd_createsprite` writes only the args it was given). **When a port stubs something out because it has no consumer, the stub is a bet on the future, so say so at the stub and re-check it when a plausible consumer arrives.** (8) **A silent no-op edit is the same defect in a third dress.** Rule (6) itself failed to apply once because a quote-escaping mismatch made `str.replace` match nothing, and nothing errored. Assert the anchor exists and verify the file changed. | `---` |

Read this doc (all of it, including the Addendum and Section 13) before starting any M17 sub-tier — it is the locked scoping source of truth, not re-derived per milestone.

Confirmed three distinct mechanic shapes: magnitude modifiers (Simple/Contrary, in `AdjustStatStage`), change-blocking gates (Clear Body/White Smoke/Hyper Cutter/Big Pecks/Keen Eye/Flower Veil, in `CanAbilityPreventStatLoss`/`AbilityPreventsSpecificStatDrop`), and reactive triggers hooking EXISTING M8/M11/M14b/M16d infrastructure rather than the stat-change pipeline itself. - M17f (Trapping check — new infrastructure — + Shadow Tag/Arena Trap/Magnet Pull): **COMPLETE** — 2026-07-02. First genuinely new-infrastructure tier since M14a — every M17a-d tier before it was pure reuse. Source: `battle_util.c :: IsAbilityPreventingEscape` (L4917-4941), called only from two selection-time sites in `battle_main.c` (the wild-battle Run menu, the party-switch-menu's `B_ACTION_SWITCH` case) — `CanBattlerEscape`, the separate function backing forced switches/faint-replacement/Baton Pass, literally has "no ability check" per its own source comment, confirming trapping is a selection-time-only gate. New `AbilityManager.is_trapped(mon, live_opponents) -> bool` encodes: a global Ghost-type exemption from all three abilities (`B_GHOSTS_ESCAPE >= GEN_6`, unconditional at this project's GEN_LATEST config); Shadow Tag's mirror-match exemption when both sides have it (`B_SHADOW_TAG_ESCAPE >= GEN_4`, also unconditional here); Arena Trap gating on `AbilityManager.is_grounded` (reused directly from M16d); Magnet Pull gating on Steel-type. New `BattleManager._get_live_opponents` mirrors `_apply_switch_in_abilities`'s existing live-opponent loop shape. Wired into `_phase_move_selection` immediately after a queued/AI-chosen switch sets `_chosen_switch_slots` — a blocked switch falls back to the mon's first move, the same fallback expression already used elsewhere in that function. Forced switches, faint replacement, and Baton Pass are confirmed unaffected by construction (none of those three call sites ever reads `_chosen_switch_slots` or calls `is_trapped` — not a special-cased exemption, just architecturally disjoint paths), and trapping only ever reads the OPPONENT's side, never the holder's own. Shed Shell (source's one item-based exemption) isn't modeled — this project has no Shed Shell item anywhere, confirmed via grep. New `m17f_test.gd`/`.tscn`: 28/28 assertions (ability data; 12 direct `is_trapped` unit tests covering every positive/negative/exemption case including a dual Ghost/Steel mon proving the Ghost exemption overrides Magnet Pull's type gate; full-battle integration for the block itself, Arena Trap's Flying exemption, Magnet Pull's Steel-only gate, Roar/Baton Pass/faint-replacement all bypassing trapping, and the holder's own side switching freely). Total assertions across all 27 numbered suites: **1476**, all green (a direct recount during this sweep found the actual suite count was already 27, not 26 as M17d's "25 prior suites" line implied — a stale count, not a regression; every suite passed clean). See `docs/decisions.md`'s `[M17f]` entry for full source citations and the Step 0 exclusion cross-check.
- M17g (Ability-suppression plumbing — new infrastructure — Mold Breaker / Neutralizing Gas): **COMPLETE** — 2026-07-03. Second genuinely new-infrastructure tier in M17. Step 0 excluded Turboblaze (163)/Teravolt (164) as legendary-exclusive (Reshiram/Kyurem-White, Zekrom/Kyurem-Black — Section 13.1), the correction M17f's own "next tier" note flagged in advance, and deferred Mycelium Might (298, a genuine hybrid whose ability-ignore half fits this tier but whose turn-order-last half needs the not-yet-built Stall shape) — final list just Mold Breaker (104) and Neutralizing Gas (256). Confirmed from source that the two abilities have fundamentally different suppression shapes and implemented each faithfully rather than sharing one mechanism: Mold Breaker is attacker-scoped and move-scoped (`moldBreakerActive` is set only while processing the Mold-Breaker holder's own current move, per `battle_util.c` L9799-9802, and never suppresses its own wielder — `CanBreakThroughAbility`'s `battlerDef == battlerAtk` exclusion, L4822-4827), and only bypasses abilities source flags `.breakable = TRUE` (26 of this project's abilities qualify — see `AbilityManager.MOLD_BREAKER_BREAKABLE`); Neutralizing Gas is field-wide and holder-presence-scoped (`IsNeutralizingGasOnField`, L4794-4803 — suppresses every OTHER live battler's ability, never its own, for as long as it's on the field). New `AbilityManager.effective_ability_id(mon, ng_active, attacker)` is the single suppression-aware chokepoint (mirrors source's `GetBattlerAbilityInternal`) that ~30 `AbilityManager` functions, 6 `StatusManager` functions, and `DamageCalculator.calculate` were all rewritten to route through instead of reading `mon.ability.ability_id` raw — confirmed via a full grep sweep, zero raw reads remain outside the primitive itself. New `AbilityManager.is_neutralizing_gas_active(combatants)` / `BattleManager._is_neutralizing_gas_active()` check the field fresh at each call site. **Retrofitted during M17h**: the `MOLD_BREAKER_BREAKABLE`/`NEUTRALIZING_GAS_UNSUPPRESSABLE` hardcoded arrays mentioned below were replaced with direct `AbilityData.breakable`/`.cant_be_suppressed` field reads after discovering `AbilityData` already had these exact fields defined and unused — see M17h's entry and `docs/decisions.md`'s `[M17g]` addendum. A source-verified correction to this tier's own task brief: Neutralizing Gas DOES suppress trapping (Shadow Tag/Arena Trap/Magnet Pull all route through the same `GetBattlerAbility` chokepoint `IsAbilityPreventingEscape` uses), but Mold Breaker does NOT (trapping is checked only at selection time, entirely outside any move-processing window) — `is_trapped` gained an `ng_active` param but deliberately no `attacker` param, documented explicitly so this doesn't get "fixed" backward later. A pre-existing, unrelated dead-code gap was found and flagged (not fixed): Ripen's ability-aware resist-berry modifier is computed correctly but never actually called by the real damage pipeline, which hardcodes the un-doubled constant instead — predates M17g, out of scope for this tier. New `m17g_test.gd`/`.tscn`: 31/31 assertions across 9 sections (ability data; `effective_ability_id`/`is_neutralizing_gas_active` direct unit tests including the NG-suppresses-Mold-Breaker-itself recursive interaction and a fainted-holder negative case; Mold Breaker bypassing a defending Levitate holder's Ground immunity via direct `DamageCalculator` calls, both the bypass itself and confirmation it doesn't apply when the Mold Breaker holder isn't the actual attacker; full-battle Neutralizing-Gas-suppresses-Intimidate and stops-once-holder-leaves scenarios; the `is_trapped()` interaction in both directions; a negative control proving the "did not fire" assertions were real discrimination, not vacuous passes). A regression-baseline discrepancy was found, surfaced to Rob, and resolved before implementation began: this file's own last-recorded total (1478, from M17f's follow-up) and the task's expected baseline (1444) both disagreed with a fresh direct recount (1454, 0 failures) — Rob confirmed proceeding on the measured 1454 baseline; root cause of the historical drift wasn't further investigated (out of scope), matching M17f's own similar "stale count, not a regression" resolution. Total assertions across all 28 `.tscn` files: 1454 prior + 31 = **1485**, all green. See `docs/decisions.md`'s `[M17g]` entry for full source citations.
- M17h (Ability-copy/overwrite plumbing — new infrastructure — Trace / Mummy / Receiver / Power of Alchemy / Wandering Spirit / Lingering Aroma): **COMPLETE** — 2026-07-03. Third genuinely new-infrastructure tier in M17. Step 0 re-verified all 6 IDs against Section 13's exclusion sweep — none needed correction, unlike the M17f→M17g handoff. Traced each ability's exact mechanic from source and kept them as genuinely separate functions rather than one shared "copy" primitive: Trace (switch-in, copies a live opponent's ability — battle_util.c L2964-3000, 50/50 random pick between two eligible doubles targets or deterministic if only one is eligible); Receiver/Power of Alchemy (doubles-only ally-fainting-triggered copy — confirmed from source these share the EXACT SAME dispatch function, `battle_script_commands.c :: BS_TryActivateReceiver` L12946-12968, not separate implementations); Mummy/Lingering Aroma (contact → one-directional overwrite of the ATTACKER's ability — confirmed mechanically identical via the same shared switch-case block, battle_util.c L3859-3883); Wandering Spirit (contact → BIDIRECTIONAL swap with the attacker, both sides reassigned, the opposite direction from Mummy's overwrite). All four read/write the RAW `.ability` field, never the suppression-aware accessor — confirmed from source, meaning a copied/traced ability is unaffected by suppression at copy time; suppression is purely a separate runtime check applied whenever the ability is later consumed (tested explicitly). A source-verified correction worth flagging: Mummy/Lingering Aroma's exemption is checked via `cant_be_suppressed` on the ATTACKER's current ability, NOT `cant_be_overwritten` as the task's own framing assumed — `cant_be_overwritten` is actually consumed by Skill-Swap/Entrainment-style moves this project doesn't have. Mid-tier design correction: discovered `AbilityData` already had `cant_be_copied`/`cant_be_swapped`/`cant_be_traced`/`cant_be_suppressed`/`cant_be_overwritten`/`breakable` fields defined and fully supported by `gen_abilities.py`, entirely unused — rather than add hardcoded arrays for M17h's own exemption needs on top of M17g's two existing arrays, all five were migrated to read directly off each ability's own `.tres` resource (a pure refactor — M17g's `m17g_test` suite re-ran unchanged at 31/31 post-retrofit). New `BattleManager.ability_changed(pokemon, new_ability_id)` signal, mirroring M16e's `type_changed` shape. New `m17h_test.gd`/`.tscn`: 64/64 assertions across 10 sections, including the bidirectional-swap confirmation (both sides checked, not just one), the doubles-targeting determinism (caught and fixed a test-authoring bug where `force_pick_second` was passed into the wrong positional parameter, silently falling back to real RNG), and the copy-time-vs-suppression-time cross-tier interaction. `.tres` data: 6 new abilities added with real source-cited descriptions (all previously empty placeholders) plus the M17g-retrofit field additions on 27 existing abilities — 114 total `.tres` files. Full regression: all 27 prior suites unchanged and still passing. Total assertions across all 29 `.tscn` files: 1485 prior + 64 = **1549**, all green. See `docs/decisions.md`'s `[M17h]` entry (and the addendum on `[M17g]`) for full source citations.

Step 0 re-verified both IDs against Section 13's exclusion sweep — neither Regenerator (144) nor Natural Cure (30) needed correction. Resolved Section 11's own hedge about splitting this tier from Wimp Out/Emergency Exit's HP-threshold forced-self-switch: confirmed from source that Regenerator/Natural Cure are purely reactive (fire only once a switch-out is already underway) while Wimp Out/Emergency Exit would need a genuinely different switch-*initiating* mechanism — the split is correct, and Wimp Out/Emergency Exit stay out of this tier entirely (deferred to a possible M17i-2). Per the `[M17h]`-established dormant-field-check discipline, confirmed neither ability needed any new/existing `AbilityData` exemption field populated — no hardcoded-array or field retrofit was needed this tier. - M17j (Item-transfer primitive — new infrastructure — Pickpocket / Sticky Hold / Magician / Symbiosis): **COMPLETE** — 2026-07-03. Fifth genuinely new-infrastructure tier in M17. Step 0 re-verified all four IDs against Section 13's exclusion sweep — none needed correction (Pickpocket's ID is defined symbolically in source, independently recounted to confirm it resolves to 124). Traced four genuinely different shapes rather than one uniform "steal" ability: Pickpocket (defender-keyed reactive, steals the attacker's item on a contact hit — folded into the existing `try_contact_effects` dispatch), Magician (genuinely attacker-keyed — the opposite direction from every existing entry in `try_contact_effects`/`try_hit_reactive_effects` — steals the target's item on any damaging hit, contact not required; needed a new top-level `try_magician` called directly from `_do_damaging_hit`), Sticky Hold (a passive blocker, not a trigger — gates whether Pickpocket/Magician's steal is allowed), Symbiosis (doubles-only voluntary give, not a steal — fires when an ally's item is removed by any means). New shared primitive `AbilityManager._try_steal_item(stealer, victim, ng_active)` mirrors source's `StealTargetItem` and is the ONE place Sticky Hold's block lives, reused by both Pickpocket and Magician rather than duplicated; Symbiosis uses a separate one-directional "give" (mirrors `BestowItem`) since Sticky Hold does NOT gate a voluntary give. Confirmed all three transfer functions reuse the existing `BattlePokemon.held_item` field directly — no parallel item-tracking mechanism. Per the `[M17h]`-established dormant-field-check discipline, confirmed no `AbilityData` field exists for "item cannot be removed" (Sticky Hold's block is a direct ability-ID check, the same precedent `[M17f]`'s trapping check set) — but source-verified that Sticky Hold DOES correctly carry the *existing* `breakable=true` flag, traced through to confirm it has no reachable consumer among these four abilities' own dispatches (would only matter for a future Knock-Off/Thief-style move, none of which exist yet) — untested-but-implemented, not a silently-dropped check. New `BattleManager.item_transferred` signal and `_try_symbiosis` wrapper (called from `_consume_item`'s single existing choke point, plus directly after Pickpocket/Magician's steals). New `m17j_test.gd`/`.tscn`: 48/48 assertions (ability data; direct unit tests for all three trigger abilities including a real `DamageCalculator.calculate()`-driven type-immunity test for Magician; full-battle Pickpocket; full-battle Sticky-Hold-blocks-Pickpocket with a source-verified role correction — Sticky Hold belongs on the ATTACKER being stolen from, since Pickpocket's holder is always the one hit; full-battle Magician; a chained doubles scenario where Magician's steal triggers Symbiosis; Neutralizing Gas suppression of all three). A quick, targeted check of `switch_test.tscn`'s long-standing unresolved flakiness (piggybacking on the m17i_test.gd bug fresh in mind) found the same superficial shape in Section 5A's post-battle field reads but confirmed it's not actually exploitable given that test's move roster — checked and ruled out, not re-fixed. Total assertions across all 31 `.tscn` files: 1584 prior + 48 = **1632**, all green. See `docs/decisions.md`'s `[M17j]` entry for full source citations.
- M17k (Priority-move-block check — new infrastructure — Dazzling / Queenly Majesty / Armor Tail): **COMPLETE** — 2026-07-03. Sixth genuinely new-infrastructure tier in M17. Step 0 re-verified all three IDs (literal, not symbolic) against Section 13's exclusion sweep — none needed correction. Confirmed from source (`IsDazzlingAbility`, battle_move_resolution.c L1499-1509) — not assumed — that all three share the exact same dispatch, genuinely identical mechanic. New `AbilityManager.blocks_priority_move(defender, defender_ally, attacker, move, ng_active)` mirrors source's `CancelerPriorityBlock`: an EXECUTION-TIME gate (dispatched before `CancelerAccuracyCheck` in source's canceler chain — confirmed via `sMoveSuccessOrderCancelers`'s fixed ordering), not a selection-time block, so the move is chosen normally and then fails, mirroring this project's existing "chosen, then fails" pattern (Roar's `no_switch_target`) rather than a pre-move `move_skipped` cancellation. Gated on `move.priority > 0` only. Confirmed SIDE-WIDE from source (matches Queenly Majesty's own "targeting the user or an ally" framing): the check covers both the move's actual target and that target's doubles partner, not holder-only — verified with a dedicated full-battle doubles test where the direct target holds no ability at all but its ally holds Dazzling, and the priority move still fails. Confirmed via `[M16d]`/`[M16e]` cross-reference that this is a structurally different concern from turn-order/speed-sorting (Trick Room, Pursuit) — no changes to `_phase_priority_resolution`'s comparator were needed. Verified the source's field-targeting-move exclusion (Trick Room/hazards) is already non-applicable here since none of this project's three field-targeting moves has positive priority — a confirmed-non-applicable simplification, not an assumed one. All three abilities carry `breakable=true`, and — unlike Sticky Hold's non-applicable case in `[M17j]` — this one is genuinely, immediately reachable (attacker and Dazzling-family holder are always different battlers), so a Mold-Breaker-holding attacker correctly bypasses the block, verified with a dedicated unit test. Per the `[M17h]`-established dormant-field-check discipline, confirmed no `AbilityData` field applies (a direct ability-ID check, same precedent as `[M17f]`'s trapping and `[M17j]`'s Sticky Hold). New `m17k_test.gd`/`.tscn`: 26/26 assertions (ability data; direct unit tests including the side-wide/fainted-ally/Mold-Breaker-bypass/Neutralizing-Gas-suppression cases; full-battle priority-blocked, priority-zero-not-blocked, side-wide doubles, holder's-own-move-unaffected, and a negative control). Baseline reconfirmed exactly at 31 files/1632 assertions before starting (no drift this time). Total assertions across all 32 `.tscn` files: 1632 prior + 26 = **1658**, all green. See `docs/decisions.md`'s `[M17k]` entry for full source citations.
- M17l (Doubles-redirect/aura abilities — Lightning Rod / Storm Drain / Friend Guard / Telepathy / Propeller Tail / Stalwart): **COMPLETE** — 2026-07-03. Unlike every tier since `[M17f]`, this one's task explicitly asked to VERIFY rather than assume "no new infrastructure" — verified directly: none was needed. Step 0 found nothing to correct (first time since `[M17d]`) — all six literal IDs clean against Section 13. Two genuinely different mechanic shapes plus a separate pair: Lightning Rod/Storm Drain are redirect-TRIGGER abilities (defender-side) that both redirect a matching-type move onto themselves (doubles only) AND fully absorb + Sp.Atk+1 whenever hit directly or by redirect (two separate source functions, `CanAbilityAbsorbMove` + `HandleMoveTargetRedirection`); Propeller Tail/Stalwart are redirect-BYPASS abilities (attacker-side, the opposite direction) — confirmed genuinely identical from source, not assumed. Telepathy (a damage exemption when the target is the attacker's own ally — source-verified NOT gated on the move being a spread move specifically, despite the flavor text) and Friend Guard (×0.75 reduction for the defender when the defender's ALLY holds it, not the holder's own damage) are a separate, unrelated pair. Checked this project's EXISTING Follow Me/Rage Powder implementation (`[M14b]`) for redirect precedence, per the task's explicit instruction — confirmed from source that Follow Me takes precedence over the ability-redirect, and Propeller Tail/Stalwart bypass both identically; wired accordingly. **No new infrastructure**: every mechanic reuses an existing pipeline hook — `absorbs_move_type`/`blocks_ally_damage` slot into `DamageCalculator`'s existing early ability-immunity gate (alongside Levitate); Friend Guard reuses the existing `defender_ally` parameter (`[M17c]`'s Flower Gift); Telepathy reuses the existing `ally` parameter (`[M17a]`'s Battery/Power Spot/Steely Spirit) with zero new plumbing; the redirect functions extend the existing Follow Me block in `_phase_move_execution` rather than adding a parallel path. Confirmed Lightning Rod/Storm Drain/Friend Guard/Telepathy all correctly carry `breakable=true` and are genuinely, immediately reachable Mold-Breaker-bypass cases (verified with dedicated tests for both the absorb and the redirect); Propeller Tail/Stalwart correctly carry no such flag. New `m17l_test.gd`/`.tscn`: 45/45 assertions across 12 sections (ability data; direct unit tests for all four mechanic shapes including Mold-Breaker-bypass and Neutralizing-Gas-suppression; full-battle doubles redirect+boost for both Lightning Rod and Storm Drain; Lightning Rod's direct-hit absorb confirmed working in singles too; Telepathy blocking an ally's attack but not an opponent's; Friend Guard's deterministic damage-reduction proof; Propeller Tail bypassing Lightning Rod's redirect — the tier's key cross-ability interaction; a negative control). Caught and fixed a real test-authoring bug during this tier (same class as `[M17j]`'s `switch_test.tscn` finding): two negative "never hit" assertions read events accumulated across the WHOLE battle rather than the specific queued turn-1 action, and failed intermittently once the original redirect target fainted in later turns and the single-move attacker legitimately retargeted the ability holder directly — fixed by filtering to each attacker's first recorded event. Stable across 8 reruns post-fix. Baseline reconfirmed exactly at 32 files/1658 assertions before starting (no drift). Total assertions across all 33 `.tscn` files: 1658 prior + 45 = **1703**, all green. See `docs/decisions.md`'s `[M17l]` entry for full source citations, including a flagged finding for M17m: Volt Absorb/Water Absorb/Sap Sipper/Flash Fire/Motor Drive/Well-Baked Body all share the exact same source dispatch (`CanAbilityAbsorbMove`) this tier's `absorbs_move_type` already partially extended.
- M17m (Absorb-family abilities — Volt Absorb / Water Absorb / Sap Sipper / Flash Fire / Motor Drive / Well-Baked Body / Earth Eater / Dry Skin's water half): **COMPLETE** — 2026-07-04. Pre-recon (`docs/m17m_absorb_recon.md`) run first, then re-verified fresh at Step 0 per standing discipline. **Scope note**: the recon's original M17m proposal was ~15 abilities (also Wonder Guard, Scrappy, Overcoat, Normalize+the "-ate" family, Mind's Eye) — this session narrowed scope to just the absorb family; those five remain unimplemented and unscheduled (see `docs/decisions.md` [M17m]'s "Next tier" section — NOT covered by M17n either). All eight route through the same source dispatch (`CanAbilityAbsorbMove`) `[M17l]`'s Lightning Rod/Storm Drain already partially extended, but split into three genuinely different on-absorb effect shapes: heal maxHP/4 (Volt Absorb/Water Absorb/Earth Eater, plus Dry Skin's previously-deferred water half — the same divisor, confirmed distinct from Dry Skin's own end-of-turn /8 tick), stat-stage boost of VARYING magnitude (Sap Sipper Atk+1, Motor Drive Speed+1 — confirmed NOT Sp.Atk despite the type overlap with Lightning Rod — Well-Baked Body Def **+2**, the tier's flagged highest-risk detail), and a persistent flag with a delayed payoff (Flash Fire — new `BattlePokemon.flash_fire_active`, cleared by `_clear_volatiles` like `minimized`/`defense_curled`; its own later Fire-move ×1.5 boost wired into the EXISTING `attack_modifier_uq412`, the same function Overgrow/Blaze/Torrent/Swarm occupy — confirmed a separate source function from the absorb dispatch itself). **Cross-cutting design decision**: widened `AbilityManager.absorbs_move_type`'s return type from a bare `int` to a `Dictionary` (`{}`/`{"kind": "stat"/"heal"/"flag", ...}`) to express all three shapes through one function, matching source's single dispatch — a deliberate breaking change to `[M17l]`'s existing contract, with its one call site and six direct unit-test assertions updated in place (`m17l_test` reran unchanged at 45/45). A second, unavoidable existing-test update: `m17c_test.gd`'s Dry Skin water-move assertion directly encoded the old "not implemented, deferred" premise as a passing test — now permanently false, so it was updated in place to assert the new absorbed-hit reality (not duplicated elsewhere; `m17c_test` reran at 79/79). New `m17m_test.gd`/`.tscn`: 63/63 assertions across 17 sections (ability data; direct `absorbs_move_type`/`attack_modifier_uq412` unit tests per group incl. Motor Drive's not-Sp.Atk and Well-Baked Body's not-+1 discriminators; Mold Breaker bypass and Neutralizing Gas suppression per group; full-battle heal-delta tests for Volt Absorb (incl. a full-HP-still-absorbs case), Water Absorb, Earth Eater, and a DEDICATED Dry Skin water-absorb test kept separate from `[M17c]`'s existing coverage; full-battle stat-boost tests for Sap Sipper/Motor Drive/Well-Baked Body; full-battle Flash Fire absorb plus a direct `DamageCalculator` comparison proving the later ×1.5 boost is real; a negative control). One anomaly investigated and ruled out: `doubles_test.tscn` failed once (53/54) with zero references to any of this tier's abilities, then reran clean 6/6 times — the same pre-existing RNG-flakiness class already documented for `switch_test.tscn`. Retroactively fixed a real pre-existing gap: Ice Ball's `ballistic_move` flag was cited in a comment since `[M16b]` but never actually set on the data dict. Air Lock confirmed as Section 13.1's established KEPT precedent (not itself excluded, despite the Rayquaza association) — re-read directly rather than assumed. Cloud Nine/Air Lock confirmed genuinely identical from source (the literal same `HasWeatherEffect` case branch, no asymmetry). Three shapes: weather-conditional Speed doublers (Swift Swim/Chlorophyll/Sand Rush, extending `[M17c]`'s Slush Rush precedent in `StatusManager.effective_speed` — a source-verified nuance NOT shared uniformly: Swift Swim/Chlorophyll additionally respect the HOLDER's own Utility Umbrella, since Umbrella only ever strips rain/sun, while Sand Rush/Slush Rush's sandstorm/hail conditions are untouched by it); weather-conditional evasion (Sand Veil/Snow Cloak, extending `[M17a]`'s Compound Eyes/Hustle precedent in `AbilityManager.accuracy_modifier_percent`, now also defender-aware); and a reactive weather-setter (Sand Spit, reusing the EXISTING `try_set_weather` Drizzle/Drought/Sand Stream already use). **The key design decision**: rather than retrofitting Air Lock/Cloud Nine awareness into every individual weather-conditional ability, new `BattleManager._effective_weather()` substitutes `WEATHER_NONE` at the small number of call sites that thread `weather` into a downstream ability function — covering `DamageCalculator.calculate` (Flower Gift/Solar Power/Dry Skin/Delta Stream, for free), `try_end_of_turn` (Rain Dish/Ice Body/Dry Skin heal, for free), the end-of-turn sandstorm/hail chip check, `try_secondary_effect` (Leaf Guard, for free), and `effective_speed`/`check_accuracy` (this tier's own abilities plus Slush Rush for free) — all without touching any of those functions' own code. Confirmed from source that weather-SETTING itself (Sand Spit, Drizzle, etc.) is unaffected by Air Lock/Cloud Nine — only weather's effects are negated — so `try_set_weather` was correctly left untouched. Caught and fixed a real flaky-test bug during reruns (not the first run): a full-battle damage-comparison test forced the damage roll but not the crit chance, so an occasional natural crit inflated damage above its forced-roll baseline — fixed by also forcing `_force_crit = false`; stable across 8 reruns after. Confirms Sandstorm is genuinely set despite Air Lock's presence (weather-SETTING is confirmed from source to be unaffected by Air Lock/Cloud Nine — only the read side, `GetWeather()`, is filtered) and that chip damage resumes the moment Air Lock leaves the field. New `m17n2_test.gd` Section 16 (12 new assertions, 58 total in the file): per-ability direct tests with a same-other-weather discriminator each, one Neutralizing-Gas-suppression test, and two full-battle confirmations (Sand Rush/sandstorm, Snow Cloak/hail) each paired with a plain-Pokémon control. - M17n-6 (Group 5: type-effectiveness-pipeline leftovers — Wonder Guard / Scrappy / Overcoat / Normalize / Refrigerate / Pixilate / Galvanize / Aerilate / Dragonize / Liquid Voice / Mind's Eye, 11 abilities): **COMPLETE** — 2026-07-05, with a same-day follow-up adding Aerilate and Dragonize. The highest-risk remaining tier in all of M17, per both `[M17l]`'s and `[M17m]`'s own advance flags — required a genuine pipeline restructure, not just a new branch. Wonder Guard's check (`AbilityManager.blocks_non_super_effective_hit`) reads the FULL combined type-effectiveness multiplier AFTER `TypeChart.get_effectiveness` computes it in `DamageCalculator.calculate`, unlike every prior ability-immunity gate (Levitate/absorb-family/Telepathy), which are flat 0x-or-nothing checks positioned BEFORE that value exists; confirmed it still blocks fixed/level-damage moves (Night Shade etc., which carry the same `power=1` placeholder as source) while correctly exempting status moves (power=0) and Struggle (TYPE_MYSTERY). Scrappy/Mind's Eye's Ghost-immunity bypass is threaded as a new `bypass_ghost_immunity` param into BOTH of this project's independent type-effectiveness computations (`TypeChart.get_effectiveness` and `get_uq412`), mirroring the Delta Stream `weaken_flying_se` precedent; Mind's Eye's second, independent half (evasion-ignore) simply extends the pre-existing `ignores_defender_evasion_stage` function, whose own doc comment had already anticipated this. Overcoat is two independent halves (powder-move immunity via the existing `blocks_move_flag`/dormant `powder_move` flag; weather-chip immunity as a new per-mon exemption alongside Air Lock/Cloud Nine's field-wide negation, confirmed non-conflicting via a dedicated composition test) — a real discrepancy was found and initially FLAGGED, not fixed, here: current reference source lists Sand Veil/Sand Force/Sand Rush/Snow Cloak as weather-chip exemptions too, directly contradicting `[M17n-2]`'s already-shipped "neither grants chip immunity" finding (**since fixed** — see `[M17n-2]`'s own status line above and its decisions.md follow-up); also flagged (still not fixed): Overcoat's un-modeled Effect Spore interaction. Normalize/Refrigerate/Pixilate/Galvanize/Liquid Voice (plus, from the same-day follow-up, Aerilate and Dragonize) mutate the MOVE's own effective type — implemented via a shallow-duplicated `MoveData` (only `.type` overridden) substituted for `DamageCalculator.calculate`'s own `move` parameter, so every existing type-aware ability/item check downstream sees the mutated type for free, with zero changes to any of them; confirmed all six power-boosting members (including Normalize itself, symmetrically) share the exact same ×1.2/UQ4.12=4915 value, and that Normalize boosts literally every move it uses (even an already-Normal one) since its own branch is unconditional on the original type, unlike the "-ate" family's. A real test-authoring bug was caught on the first run: comparing a Pixilate'd/Liquid-Voice'd move's damage against a single-Normal-typed attacker confounds the power-boost measurement with a STAB loss (mutating away from the attacker's own type loses STAB) — fixed by using a dual-typed attacker so STAB holds constant across the comparison. **Follow-up (same day)**: Aerilate (184, Mega-exclusivity exclusion reversed by Rob) and Dragonize (312) added, reusing this tier's exact infrastructure — Dragonize's own ID was flagged BEFORE implementing, since direct source inspection shows it sitting in `pokeemerald_expansion`'s own cluster of 6 hack-project-only custom ability slots (`m17_recon.md` Section 8.3's original exclusion, independently re-confirmed: no `aiRating` field, flanked by two literal blank `"-------"` placeholder slots and two abilities whose source description is literally `"Unimplemented."`); Rob confirmed implementing it anyway as a deliberate override (Dragonize has since become real in a newer generation than this reference tree models). New `m17n6_test.gd`/`.tscn`: 101/101 assertions across 22 sections (95 original + 6 from the follow-up), stable across 8 reruns (original) and 5 reruns (follow-up). Baseline reconfirmed exactly at 39 files/2071 assertions before starting (no drift). Targeted regression (`ability_test`/`m17a_test`/`m17m_test`/`m17n2_test`) plus two full 40-file sweeps (original + follow-up) all passed unchanged (0 real failures — one grep false-positive on `stat_test.tscn`'s own "fail at +6 max"-style test labels, confirmed harmless). Total assertions across all 40 `.tscn` files: 2071 prior + 95 + 6 = **2172**, all green. See `docs/decisions.md`'s `[M17n-6]` entry (and its same-day follow-up subsection) for full source citations.
- M17n-7 (Group 6: item/berry interaction — Klutz / Unnerve / Gluttony / Unburden / Harvest / Cud Chew): **COMPLETE** — 2026-07-06, a recovery-and-completion session (a prior session's implementation work was found already in the working tree, uncommitted, with no test file or decisions.md entry — re-verified from scratch against `include/constants/abilities.h` and source rather than trusted at face value). Step 0 confirmed all six IDs clean; none carry `breakable`/`cant_be_suppressed`. Klutz (`ItemManager.effective_held_item`, the single held-item chokepoint every other function already routes through) and Unnerve (blocks ALL berry effects via source's single `ItemBattleEffects` dispatcher gate, not just resist berries — already correctly scoped in the inherited code) both verified correct as found. Gluttony confirmed a no-op for this project's entire current item roster (Sitrus's fraction is hardcoded to 2 regardless of ability), wired in generically per the Sticky-Hold precedent. Unburden's unconditional Speed ×2 (`battle_main.c` L4686-4687) verified wired into `StatusManager.effective_speed`, activated via `CheckSetUnburden`'s every-item-removal-site pattern. Harvest finally builds the "last consumed berry" tracker `[M17d]` deferred twice — `BattlePokemon.last_consumed_berry`, confirmed against `include/battle.h`'s `struct PartyState` to be genuinely switch-persistent (unlike Unburden/Cud Chew's own switch-cleared volatiles). **A real bug was found and fixed** (not merely inherited-and-confirmed like the rest of this tier): Cud Chew's re-trigger sets source's `overrideBerryRequirements` flag, which makes BOTH the HP-threshold check AND the Unnerve check return unconditionally-bypassed (`battle_util.c` L5465, L338-339) — the inherited `sitrus_berry_heal`/`lum_berry_cures` calls still applied both gates unconditionally even with `override_item` set. Fixed by gating both checks on `override_item == null`, preserving only the one source-verified exception (no heal at exactly full HP even under override). New `m17n7_test.gd`/`.tscn`: 62/62 assertions across 13 sections including a dedicated discriminating test for the bug fix (Section 10: the bypass itself plus a without-override negative control proving it wasn't vacuous). Two test-authoring bugs caught and fixed on the first run (59/62): an out-of-domain Gluttony fraction test, and hardcoded (rather than dynamically read) Speed values for the Unburden test. A baseline discrepancy was found during this session and initially "resolved" by adopting a fresh recount of 2160 — **that figure was itself wrong**, confirmed by a dedicated follow-up diagnostic session (2026-07-06) that root-caused the recurring drift: `scenes/battle/integration_test.tscn` (24 real, always-passing assertions) prints a third result format (`"Integration tests: N passed, M failed"`) that every ad-hoc recount so far — including this tier's own 2160 figure — failed to recognize, silently dropping its 24 assertions. See CLAUDE.md's testing-conventions section for the full mechanism and the standing rule this established. Full regression: all 40 prior files pass unchanged (`item_test.tscn`, whose call sites this session's fix directly touched, reran clean at 77/77). **VERIFIED: 2246 total assertions across 41 `.tscn` files**, confirmed via two independent methods (`scripts/count_assertions.sh` against a fresh sweep, and a per-file instrumented-source cross-check) and reproducible across two independent clean runs (2026-07-06). See `docs/decisions.md`'s `[M17n-7]` entry for full source citations.
- M17n-8 (Group 8, sub-tier 1: contact/faint-timing + reactive/one-off — Aftermath / Innards Out / Corrosion / Merciless / Opportunist): **COMPLETE** — 2026-07-06. Step 0 confirmed all five IDs clean against `include/constants/abilities.h`; Perish Body (blocked on the unimplemented Perish Song move) and Suction Cups (deferred) explicitly excluded from this sub-tier per Rob's instruction, not silently dropped. None of the five carry `breakable`/`cant_be_suppressed`. Aftermath/Innards Out share one mechanism (`AbilityManager.faint_retaliation_damage`, wired into `_phase_faint_check` alongside Destiny Bond/Moxie's existing `_last_attacker` killer-lookup) but differ in two source-verified ways: Aftermath requires contact and is blocked by any Damp holder on the field (new `is_damp_active`, NG-aware per source's `GetBattlerAbility`-routed `IsAbilityOnField`); Innards Out has neither restriction and deals the fainted mon's own HP immediately before the fatal hit (new `_last_attacker_hp_before`/`_last_attacker_move` companion trackers), not a fixed fraction — confirmed via a deliberate overkill full-battle test. Corrosion bypasses Poison/Steel-type poison immunity via the attacker's own ability (`bypasses_poison_steel_immunity`, mirroring Scrappy's `bypasses_ghost_immunity` precedent), closing a gap M3's own code comment flagged since this project's earliest milestone. **A second, genuinely independent bug was found and fixed** while writing Corrosion's full-battle test: `_phase_move_execution`'s own general "type immunity check for foe-targeting moves" ALSO blocks Toxic (Poison-type) against a Steel-type target (a real, separate 0x type-chart immunity, correct for cases like Thunder Wave vs. Ground) — entirely independent of the status-specific check Corrosion was wired into. Source confirmed `ABILITY_CORROSION` appears exactly once in the whole reference tree, and its failure branch reuses the same "doesn't affect" script a flat type immunity does — meaning real source resolves this through the ONE status-specific check with no separate downstream gate for this purpose. Fixed by threading the same Corrosion check into that general gate, scoped narrowly to Poison-type moves only. Merciless is a guaranteed (not stage-bonus) crit vs. a poisoned/toxic'd target, tested via a 30-trial statistical sample mirroring `[M17n-5]`'s rate-testing pattern. Opportunist copies an opponent's stat INCREASE only (never decreases, never self-triggers by construction — opponents-only scope) at the same primary move-driven stat-change site `[M17b]`'s Defiant/Competitive already occupy; deliberately not gated on `move.stat_change_self` (source cares which side rose, not whether the move was self-targeted) and confirmed no infinite-loop risk (the copy calls `apply_stat_change` directly, never re-entering the reactive dispatch). Known simplification, documented: wired into this one call site only, not retrofitted into every `apply_stat_change` call site — ability-driven raises (Moxie, Weak Armor, Download) and Baton-Pass/Psych-Up copies aren't covered. A real test-authoring bug (infinite-battle deadlock from a Swords-Dance-only moveset) was caught and fixed on the first run (55/58). New `m17n8_test.gd`/`.tscn`: 58/58 assertions across 11 sections, stable across 8 reruns. Full regression (direct foreground sweep, `pkill -9` first, `scripts/count_assertions.sh` against fresh output, re-run twice from a clean state): all 41 prior files pass unchanged, 0 real failures both runs. Total assertions across all 42 `.tscn` files: 2246 prior + 58 = **2304**, confirmed via `count_assertions.sh` and reproducible across both runs. See `docs/decisions.md`'s `[M17n-8]` entry for full source citations.

Deliberately NOT blocked, confirmed from source: Struggle's fixed recoil and `[M17n-8]`'s own Aftermath/Innards-Out retaliation against the killer (both gated only by other mechanisms in source, never Magic Guard) — plus Toxic Spikes' poison infliction itself (only the resulting residual damage is gated). Confirmed from source and tested explicitly: Magic Bounce's check sits BEFORE the Dark-type Prankster-immunity gate, so a Prankster'd status move against a Dark-type Magic Bounce holder correctly bounces rather than being eaten as a no-op; `.breakable = TRUE` in source (the one exception among this tier's three abilities) — a Mold-Breaker attacker's status move is NOT reflected.
