**M18 status: fully complete in every sense — implementation, testing, and pipeline migration.** Every flagged-but-unfixed item found across the whole M18 effort is recorded in the `[M18.5a]` and `[M21]` entries below; all six are now resolved (four via `[M18.5a]`, the remaining two via `[M21]`).

- M18.5a (Post-M18 technical debt — Poison Touch fixes + 2 test-authoring bugs, 4 items): **COMPLETE** — 2026-07-08. Closed Post-M18 Review items 1, 2, 5, and 6. **Items 1+2 (Poison Touch)**: confirmed via direct source read (`ABILITYEFFECT_MOVE_END_ATTACKER`, battle_util.c L4281-4299 — an explicitly-commented "same as above, but for attacker" SEPARATE dispatch pass) that Poison Touch is ATTACKER-keyed and poisons the DEFENDER, unlike every other ability in `try_contact_effects` (all defender-keyed reactions to being hit, Poison Point included, confirmed still correct via its own `CanBePoisoned` argument order). Fixed by checking Poison Touch independently before `id` is even computed (so a defender with no ability doesn't block it), gated by the same Shield Dust/Covert Cloak check `[M18x]` already established — checked against the DEFENDER (the poison recipient), the same battler role `StatusManager.try_secondary_effect`'s existing gate uses. Flagged, not fixed: a rare double-ability-holder edge case (attacker holds Poison Touch AND defender independently holds Poison Point) where only one of the two fires, since this function's single-effect-per-call return shape has no way to report both. **Items 5+6 (found during `[M18-cleanup]`'s regression sweep)**: both confirmed TEST bugs via direct debug tracing, zero production code touched for either. Item 5 (`m17n7_test.gd` S8.07/S11.01, Harvest/Cud Chew): the file's own `_make_item` helper predates `[M18-patch-1]`'s `pocket` field and never set it, so every berry it constructs fails `_consume_item`'s `item.pocket == POCKET_BERRIES` gate — `last_consumed_berry` silently never gets set even though the berry's own heal effect fires correctly, starving both abilities of anything to regenerate/re-fire. Fixed by adding a `pocket` param to the helper and passing `POCKET_BERRIES` at all 11 genuine-berry call sites. Item 6 (`m18q_test.gd` Q02.09, Shell Bell): NOT the M17n-2-shaped "missing forced crit" hypothesis in the literal sense assumed, but adjacent — direct debug tracing showed the fixture's non-crit forced-max-roll hit (56 dmg) couldn't one-shot its target (61 max HP, per `[M18r]`'s own `+level+10` floor finding), so the target survived to counter-attack and legitimately dent the holder below max HP before a later, correctly-firing heal was misread as a bug — a fresh recurrence of the whole-battle-aggregation pitfall. Fixed by adding `_force_crit = true` (1.5× pushes 56→84, exceeding 61), mirroring the same file's own already-established forced-roll-plus-forced-crit sibling test. New discriminators added to `m17c_test.gd` (Poison Point/Touch's own origin suite — S5.03 corrected direction, S5.03b/c/d/e new): 85/85 (was 79). Regression: `m18x_test.tscn` 15/15, `m17n1_test.tscn` 82/82, `item_registry_test.tscn` 309/309, `m17n7_test.tscn` 62/62, `m18q_test.tscn` 16/16 — all unchanged/fixed as expected, stable across 3-4 reruns each. Post-M18 Review's remaining items 3+4 (Shell Bell doubles gaps) stay correctly deferred to M22. Recommend **M18.5d (Gender), M18.5f (Binding-move), M18.5g (Multi-hit), or M18.5h (Nature/IV/EV)** — all four remaining Phase 1 tracks are independent and dependency-free at this point, per Rob's preference.

- M18.5d Phase 1 (Gender infrastructure): **COMPLETE** — 2026-07-08. The one genuine hard dependency in M18.5's Phase 1 — Attract (M18.5e) was blocked on this. Two real Step-0 findings reshaped scope: (1) most of the "extraction pipeline" work was already done — `data/pokemon.json` already carries an accurate `gender_ratio` field for all 386 species (spot-checked against source for 5 categories: Bulbasaur 31/skewed-starter, Rattata 127/50-50, Chansey 254/always-female, Ditto 255/genderless, Tyrogue 0/always-male — all exact), and `PokemonSpecies.gender_ratio` already exists in the schema with a correct doc comment — both dormant since `[M15]`, the same "unpopulated schema field" shape `ItemData.pocket` had before `[M18-patch-1]`. The Python extractor itself (`tools/convert_pokedata.py`, per `[M15]`'s own decisions.md entry) doesn't exist anywhere in this repo — unlike `gen_items.py`/`gen_moves.py`/`gen_abilities.py`, it was never kept as a rerunnable generator — so there was nothing to "extend"; also confirmed `data/pokemon/` (the would-be per-species `.tres` directory) is empty and no JSON-to-`PokemonSpecies`-Resource converter exists anywhere in production code — species data lives only as bulk JSON + `PokemonRegistry`'s dictionary API, a pre-existing architectural gap flagged, not built. (2) the task's own "mirrors how IVs are already handled" assumption was WRONG — `from_species` hardcodes `ivs = [0,0,0,0,0,0]` unconditionally (a deliberate M1-era placeholder per the field's own doc comment) and contains zero `randi()` calls anywhere, so there was no existing "roll once at creation" pattern to mirror; designed fresh instead. New `BattlePokemon.gender: int` (clean `GENDER_MALE/FEMALE/GENDERLESS` enum, matching this project's own `STATUS_*`/`STAGE_*` style rather than reusing source's raw 0/254/255 sentinel bytes), rolled once in `from_species` via new `_roll_gender()`, porting `GetGenderFromSpeciesAndPersonality` (pokemon.c L1847-1861) exactly — the three sentinels short-circuit with no roll, everything else is `gender_ratio > randi() % 256`. No forcing seam added — `gender` is freely reassignable post-construction like every other field, matching this project's ~70 existing `_make_mon`-style fixture helpers; a future Attract test should just set it directly. Confirmed zero existing ability/item logic reads gender anywhere (grep, zero hits outside the schema declaration) — a genuine greenfield addition, nothing needed immediate gender-awareness. New `m18_5d_test.tscn`: 11/11 (5 data-integrity + 6 instance-generation, including n=2000 statistical-rate checks for a skewed and a 50/50 species matching `[M17n-5]`/`[M18e]`'s tolerance-band convention), stable across 5 reruns. Regression: smoke test unchanged (386 species), `battle_test`/`damage_test` 24/24/`status_test` 78/78/`move_test` 49/49/`stat_test` 78/78 (all `from_species` consumers with fixed IV/EV) — all unchanged, confirming the new `randi()` call doesn't disturb existing determinism. **M18.5e (Attract) is now unblocked.** Recommend **M18.5e (Attract, now unblocked)**, or **M18.5f (Binding-move)/M18.5g (Multi-hit)/M18.5h (Nature/IV/EV)** (still independent, no dependency change), per Rob's preference.

- M18.5d Phase 2 (Gender-dependent mechanics — Attract, Rivalry, Cute Charm, Oblivious, 4 items): **COMPLETE** — 2026-07-08. - M18.5d-3 (Infatuation source tracking): **COMPLETE** — 2026-07-08. Closes the one gap `[M18.5d Phase 2]` deliberately flagged: infatuation previously only cured on the INFATUATED mon's own switch-out, missing real source's reciprocal condition — the infatuated mon is ALSO cured the instant the Pokémon who attracted it leaves the field (switch-out or faint), even if the infatuated mon itself never switched. Confirmed via source (`INFATUATED_WITH(battler) = battler + 1`, a raw slot-index encoding driven by C's bitfield constraints) that this project didn't need to reproduce that raw-index shape — `BattlePokemon.infatuated: bool` replaced with `infatuated_by: BattlePokemon = null` (a direct object reference), matching this project's own existing `_last_attacker` dictionary precedent for "who did this to me" tracking rather than inventing a new pattern. Confirmed source's two separate trigger functions (`SwitchInClearSetData`/`FaintClearSetData`, both battle_main.c) collapse cleanly into this project's ONE existing `_clear_volatiles(mon)` chokepoint (already called at all 4 real "a battler left the field" moments — regular faint, Destiny-Bond-triggered faint, Aftermath/Innards-Out-triggered faint, and switch-out) — added a single reciprocal scan there (loop `_combatants`, clear anyone else's `infatuated_by` if it points at the mon that just left), rather than two separate insertion points. Doubles confirmed a non-factor requiring no new infrastructure (the scan works generically) but also not specifically tested, consistent with the project's "don't build unreachable doubles coverage prematurely" precedent (Shell Bell). Extended `m18_5d2_test.gd`'s existing Attract section (no new file) — 3 new assertions: source-battler-leaves cures the victim (the fix itself), an unrelated third battler leaving does NOT cure it (discriminator), and fainting the source also cures it (confirms both real trigger conditions). The holder's own switch-out cure was explicitly reconfirmed as a regression check, not assumed. **49/49** (was 46/46), stable across 5 reruns. Regression: `item_registry_test.tscn` 309/309, `status_test.tscn` 78/78 — both unchanged. - M18.5f (Binding-move mechanic): **COMPLETE** — 2026-07-08. 10 moves, not the 11 `docs/m19_recon.md` claimed — Bind/Wrap/Fire Spin/Clamp/Whirlpool/Sand Tomb/Magma Storm/Infestation/Snap Trap/Thunder Cage all share the identical real-source `MOVE_EFFECT_WRAP` mechanic; **Jaw Lock is excluded**, a direct source read shows it dispatches `MOVE_EFFECT_TRAP_BOTH` instead — a completely different, zero-damage, permanent, bidirectional trap (the Mean Look/Block family's `escapePrevention`), conflated by the recon on flavor-text similarity alone. Confirmed binding does NOT restrict move selection (absent from every pre-move canceler in source) — only blocks voluntary switching and deals maxHP/8 recurring end-of-turn damage for a random 4-5 turns. Reused the EXISTING generic `secondary_effect`/`secondary_chance` fields (`SE_WRAP`) rather than a bespoke move flag — cheaper than Attract's own dedicated dispatch, since binding is a damage move with an attached generic effect, not a status move. New `BattlePokemon.wrapped_by`/`wrapped_turns`; `AbilityManager.is_trapped()` extended with a `wrapped_by` check right after its existing Ghost-type gate (a Ghost-type still takes the recurring damage, only the switch-block exemption applies); `BattleManager._clear_volatiles` extended with the exact same `[M18.5d-3]`-pattern reciprocal cross-battler scan — the source battler leaving the field also cures the victim's trap, confirmed via the identical two source functions `[M18.5d-3]` already unified. Confirmed a genuine off-by-one in the duration counter (checked BEFORE decrementing in source, so an N-turn trap deals N damage ticks then one silent free "ends" tick) and reproduced it exactly rather than assuming the simpler decrement-then-clear shape `disable_turns`/`encore_turns` already use. Found and avoided a real correctness pitfall: SE_WRAP was given its own dispatch branch (same shape as SE_FLINCH's existing carve-out) rather than falling into the shared status/confusion-cure-berry branch, which would have spuriously evaluated an unrelated pre-existing status against a held cure berry. New `m18_5f_test.gd`/`.tscn`: 137/137, stable across 6 reruns (one intermittent accuracy-roll flake caught and fixed via `bm._force_hit = true`, not preemptively guessed). Regression: `item_registry_test.tscn` 309/309, `status_test.tscn` 78/78, `m17n9_test.tscn` (Magic Guard's own origin suite) 63/63, plus `m17f_test.tscn` 30/30 and `m18_5d2_test.tscn` 49/49 (both directly-extended functions' own origin suites, beyond the named regression scope). **Grip Claw is now unblocked** (7-turn duration extension) but still deferred to M18.5i's reconsideration pass, same for Binding Band (maxHP/6 variant) — neither item is built here. Recommend **M18.5g (Multi-hit) or M18.5h (Nature/IV/EV)** — both remain independent and dependency-free.
- M18.5g (Multi-hit move mechanism): **COMPLETE** — 2026-07-08. 30 moves — confirmed via direct source grep, matching `docs/m19_recon.md`'s count of 31 exactly this time; **Population Bomb is excluded** — the one `.strikeCount` move with per-hit accuracy checks AND a uniquely-shaped Loaded Dice range, a genuinely higher complexity class than the other 30, flagged for a future tier. Roll distribution confirmed exact: **35%/35%/15%/15%** (2/3/4/5 hits) for this project's default Gen5+ config — a real correction to the commonly-cited 37.5/37.5/12.5/12.5 figure, which is actually the older pre-Gen5 branch of the same source function. Triple Kick/Triple Axel (`is_triple_kick`) each independently roll accuracy per hit (unlike every other move in the family, which checks once) and escalate power ×1/×2/×3; Scale Shot (`is_scale_shot`) applies a one-time self stat change once after the whole sequence, not per hit. Refactored `BattleManager._do_damaging_hit` from `void` to `int` (returns real damage dealt) plus a new `suppress_shell_bell` param, since **Shell Bell must heal ONCE from the damage ACCUMULATED across the whole sequence, not per hit** — confirmed via source's `savedDmg +=` accumulation; a per-hit heal would under-heal due to floor-division truncation. Every other per-hit mechanism (contact abilities, King's Rock, the survive-lethal-hit chain, hit-reactive abilities, Twineedle's own per-hit poison chance) fires correctly for free simply by calling `_do_damaging_hit` once per loop iteration, confirmed individually rather than assumed uniform. Mid-sequence termination verified as three genuinely different shapes: target fainting stops immediately; a Substitute absorbs MULTIPLE hits before breaking (continues, unlike fainting) and only stops the sequence the instant it actually breaks; a wholly-immune/ability-absorbed hit stops after just one attempt. Found and fixed two small, genuinely in-scope pre-existing gaps: `SE_POISON` didn't exist at all (only `SE_TOXIC`), needed for Twineedle's real (non-toxic) poison chance — also corrected a mislabeled `_status_to_se` mapping this surfaced (Poison Point/Poison Touch's `secondary_applied` signal was silently reporting regular poison as Toxic); `strike_count`/`multi_hit`/`always_critical_hit` were never wired into `gen_moves.py`'s own `DEFAULTS`/`FIELD_ORDER` at all, meaning no hand-authored move entry could have ever actually emitted them to a `.tres` file before this fix. Skill Link/Loaded Dice are now unblocked but not implemented — mechanism-only scope, matching Grip Claw's own precedent from `[M18.5f]`. New `m18_5g_test.gd`/`.tscn`: 315/315, stable across 6 reruns, sectioned by mechanism concern per the task's own instruction (only Triple Kick/Axel get a dedicated section). Regression treated as a wide sweep (matching `[M18t]`'s own scoping, not a routine 2-3-suite check, given how many existing mechanisms the `_do_damaging_hit` refactor touches): 18 suites, all clean — `item_registry_test` 309/309, `damage_test` 24/24, `move_test` 49/49, `stat_test` 78/78, `tier3_test` 62/62, `tier4_test` 86/86, `m17c_test` 85/85, `m17j_test` 48/48, `m17n5_test` 78/78, `m17n8_test` 58/58, `m17n9_test` 63/63, `m18k_test` 16/16, `m18q_test` 16/16, `m18d_test` 19/19, `m18p_test` 33/33, `m18o_test` 19/19, `m18_5f_test` 137/137, `m18_5d2_test` 49/49. Recommend **M18.5h (Nature/IV/EV)** as the next tier — the last of the three independent M18.5 Phase 1 tracks, now that binding and multi-hit are both complete.

Second of two M18.5h sub-tiers — **M18.5h is now fully complete** (EV gain remains deferred to M20; likes/dislikes remain excluded, both per Rob's own scope decisions on the recon). Corrected a factual error in the task's own framing: its cited "`[M18.5h-1]` UQ_4_12 truncation-rounding lesson" does not exist in that entry — Nature used plain `floori()` truncation, not UQ_4_12 fixed-point math. Re-verified the combined stat formula directly against `pokemon.c` L1406-1425 and found it **already 100% correct** in `_stat_formula`/`_hp_formula` since Milestone 1 — **zero formula changes needed anywhere**; this tier's entire surface is `from_species` + one new `_roll_ivs()` function. 6 INDEPENDENT `randi() % 32` rolls (source's real IVs come from a separate random "IV word," not personality — same reproduce-the-distribution-not-the-bit-packing precedent as gender/nature). **New `forced_ivs: Variant = null` parameter on `from_species`**, resolving an explicit design question beyond simple all-or-nothing forcing: accepts either a fully-concrete `Array[int]` (all 6 forced) OR a per-stat-nullable `Array` (SOME stats forced, others still roll normally) — directly matching M24's real future need for competitively-built trainer Pokémon with some stats maxed and the rest left alone. Sweep 1 still found 7 more files (`damage_test.gd`, missed from the proactive batch, plus 6 suites — including `integration_test.gd` — that `[M18.5h-1]`'s own regression never touched at all, since IV has NO neutral no-op case the way Nature's 5/25 chance provided, so nothing was ever "lucky" under IV). Sweep 2: 100% clean across all 76 suites. 31 test files touched total this session (listed in full in the `[M18.5h-2]` decisions.md entry) plus `battle_pokemon.gd`. `forced_nature` and `forced_ivs` (including partial per-stat forcing) are both now ready for M24 (Trainer Data) to consume whenever that milestone starts. Recommend **M18.5i** (the Grip Claw/Binding Band/Destiny Knot reconsideration pass, per its own already-established deferral point in `[M18.5f]`'s and `[M18.5d Phase 2]`'s entries) as a natural next tier, though Rob's own preference governs sequencing from here.

- NEW ITEM D scoping (Shared Accuracy Roll Architecture Gap — recon only, no code/tests): **COMPLETE** — 2026-07-16. Re-derives from source, corrects and RAISES the severity of NEW ITEM A's own original framing (which had assumed, without verifying, that source might share this project's single-shared-accuracy-roll simplification — it does not). Confirmed via direct citation that source resolves BOTH ordinary accuracy (`CancelerAccuracyCheck`, `battle_move_resolution.c:2174-2260`, its own explicit per-battler loop calling `DoesMoveMissTarget` independently, reading each target's own evasion stage via `GetTotalAccuracy`) AND the semi-invulnerable bypass (a separate, structurally identical per-target canceler loop, `battle_move_resolution.c:1960-2010`, `CanBreakThroughSemiInvulnerablity` called independently per target) via DEDICATED PER-TARGET LOOPS — this project's own single shared `StatusManager.check_accuracy` call (`battle_manager.gd:2658`, before the spread/single split) is a confirmed, genuine divergence, not shared upstream behavior. Traced current behavior precisely: a miss on the single shared roll aborts the WHOLE move (zero targets hit); a hit unconditionally passes EVERY live target to `_do_damaging_hit()` with no further per-target accuracy/semi-invulnerable check at all (confirmed via its full body) — a strict all-or-nothing binary, no partial-hit outcome is currently possible. Neither `check_accuracy` nor `_can_hit_semi_invulnerable` need logic changes (both already stateless and per-target-capable) — the gap is purely a call-site scoping issue. Exact affected-move count queried directly (not estimated): **59 currently-implemented `is_spread=True` damage-category moves** (not the "~37" originally estimated — that predated NEW ITEM A/C's own pool growth). Two concrete player-visible impact classes identified: a high-frequency case (any two opposing targets with different evasion/accuracy-modifying state get an architecturally-impossible-to-diverge shared outcome) and a lower-frequency, higher-severity case (a spread move vs. one semi-invulnerable + one grounded target can wrongly hit the semi-invulnerable one OR wrongly block the grounded one, depending on which the project's own default-target logic happens to check) — not empirically reproduced this session (recon-only), but a direct conclusion from the traced code paths. Blast-radius assessed as a contained core fix (wrap the existing, unchanged per-target-capable checks in a loop) with real surrounding bookkeeping needing its own design pass first (`move_missed`'s per-move signal shape, `crashes_on_miss`'s unresolved partial-spread-miss semantics, Blunder Policy's per-target trigger point) — secondary effects (flinch/stat-lowering/status) confirmed unaffected, already correctly per-target. Cross-referenced against the turn-order-splice trio/Acupressure/Lightning-Rod-Storm-Drain-redirect: independent, only a soft thematic overlap with Dragon Darts' own per-hit-miss concept. **Per explicit instruction, this session stops short of a firm priority recommendation and flags the raised severity for Rob's own input** before any future session scopes implementation — three candidate placements identified (own dedicated session; folded into the turn-order-splice session; deprioritized), no default chosen. - NEW ITEM D implementation (Shared Accuracy Roll Architecture Gap — Step 0 + implementation): **COMPLETE** — 2026-07-16, same-day follow-up to the scoping session above. Step 0 re-verified fresh (not trusted from the scoping session) and resolved all 6 open design questions cleanly, no genuine tangle: `crashes_on_miss` (Jump Kick/High Jump Kick/Axe Kick/Supercell Slam) confirmed via direct source read to be `.target=TARGET_SELECTED` for all 4 — never co-occurs with `is_spread`, a non-issue; `recoil_percent`/`drain_percent`/`is_rage`/`is_recharge` are all already gated on `damage > 0` inside `_do_damaging_hit` (called once per target), composing correctly for free once a missed target is simply skipped; `is_rollout`/`is_fury_cutter`/`is_steel_beam`/`is_rampage`/`is_uproar` also confirmed via `gen_moves.py` grep to never co-occur with `is_spread`, so the pre-existing shared miss-handling block is simply and safely skipped for spread moves; Dragon Darts' smart-target mechanism dispatches through the separate `multi_hit`/`strike_count` branch, confirmed untouched; `StatusManager.check_accuracy` (already calling its own internal `_can_hit_semi_invulnerable` per its `defender` param) needed zero logic changes — a pure call-site scoping fix; Blunder Policy resolved as a disclosed simplification (fires only when a spread move's accuracy roll misses EVERY live target, matching `move_missed`'s own new single-shot threshold), via a new shared `_apply_blunder_policy_on_miss` helper reused by both the pre-existing single-target path and the new spread path. Implementation: the old single shared accuracy-check block is now guarded to skip spread moves entirely (`if not (move.is_spread and _active_per_side > 1):`); each live target (opponents + ally, if `target_includes_ally`) now gets its own independent `StatusManager.check_accuracy` call inside the spread-dispatch loop before `_do_damaging_hit` runs for it, mirroring source's real per-battler `CancelerAccuracyCheck` loop — a miss excludes only that one target, others in the same use resolve normally. New `move_missed_target(attacker, target, reason)` signal fires per individual miss; the existing `move_missed` signal stays single-shot, firing only on a full "every target missed" spread use (preserving `_current_action_failed`'s Stomping-Tantrum-timer semantics). Confirmed composes correctly with `[M21]`'s own Shell Bell/Life Orb spread-accumulation fix — a missed target simply never reaches `_do_damaging_hit`, contributing 0 to the accumulated total by construction. Test-audit-first pass found zero existing assertions needed fixing (every spread-move test in this codebase already used `_force_hit` or a hardcoded `accuracy=100`, both behaviorally identical whether accuracy is checked once or once-per-target). New `scenes/battle/new_item_d_test.gd`/`.tscn`: 18/18 assertions, stable across 5 reruns — a fully-deterministic semi-invulnerable+grounded independence proof (Earthquake hits both a grounded and a mid-Dig target in one spread use; Rock Slide, lacking `damages_underground`, hits only the grounded one), partial-miss-vs-full-miss signal-shape discriminators, Blunder Policy's full-miss-only threshold, a 60-trial statistical evasion-divergence proof (0-evasion target hits 100% of trials independent of a +6-evasion target's own ~33% rate), Shell Bell accumulation excluding a missed target's contribution, and a singles negative control. Step 0 individually re-verified all 67 of Bucket 1's moves against `moves_info.h` with a broader flag scan than the original classifier used (added `.alwaysCriticalHit`, `.damagesAirborne`, `.pulseMove`, `.windMove`, `.ignoresTargetAbility`, `.ignoresTargetDefenseEvasionStages`, `.cantUseTwice`, and `.priority`, none of which the classifier had extracted) — matching `[M19a-gen1]`'s own precedent of not trusting a "pure data-entry" classification blindly. **6 of the 67 were found to need a genuinely new mechanism** and moved to Bucket 4 as three new sub-groups: Chip Away(498)/Sacred Sword(533)/Darkest Lariat(626) (`ignoresTargetDefenseEvasionStages` — no bypass path exists in `DamageCalculator`'s stat-stage application), Sunsteel Strike(667)/Moongeist Beam(668) (`ignoresTargetAbility` — `AbilityManager.effective_ability_id()` only bypasses on the ATTACKER's own Mold Breaker/Mycelium Might, not a per-move flag), Blood Moon(829) (`cantUseTwice` — no move-repeat tracking exists). Two flags that looked like new mechanisms turned out to be safe reuses: `alwaysCriticalHit` (already-registered `always_critical_hit` field, M18.5g precedent) and `pulseMove` (already-registered `pulse_move` field, wired to Mega Launcher — and per Mega Launcher's own implementation comment, this tier's Aura Sphere/Dragon Pulse/Origin Pulse are the FIRST real moves in the roster ever to carry `pulse_move=true`, closing a "only tested via synthetic MoveData" gap). Also caught: 10 of the 61 confirmed-pure moves carry nonzero `priority` (Mach Punch +1, Vital Throw −1, Extreme Speed +2, plus 7 more at +1) — an existing field the original Bucket 1 classification never extracted, which would have silently defaulted to 0 without this check. **61 confirmed genuinely pure data-entry and implemented**, each using only already-wired generic fields — zero new `battle_manager.gd`/`status_manager.gd`/`damage_calculator.gd`/`ability_manager.gd` dispatch logic added. New `m19_bucket1_test.gd`/`.tscn`: parameterized table-driven suite (single loop over all 61 moves, not 61 individual functions), 736/736 assertions, passed clean on first run — Section A data-integrity spot-checks (core data + every flag token + negative checks for every flag NOT carried); Section B functional plumbing checks (Dragon Claw deals real damage through the dispatch path; Megahorn's `makes_contact` triggers Rough Skin, Aura Sphere's absence of it doesn't — discriminator; Dragon Pulse's `pulse_move` deals strictly more damage with Mega Launcher than without — first real-data exercise of that dispatch line). `critical_hit_stage`/`damages_airborne`/`priority` deliberately left as data-only checks, matching `[M19a-gen1]`'s established testing-scope convention (force_crit can't observe crit-stage math; semi-invulnerable bypass covered by `two_turn_test.gd`; general priority-ordering covered by `battle_test.gd`). Regression: `item_registry_test.tscn` 309/309, `status_test.tscn` 78/78, `stat_test.tscn` 78/78, `damage_test.tscn` 24/24 — all unchanged, narrow scope per task instruction. **Total move-implementation count: 155→216.** `docs/m19_subtier_plan.md` updated throughout: Bucket 1 marked COMPLETE (61 implemented + 6 moved to Bucket 4, which grows 39→45 moves/18→21 sub-groups), Section A/E tables and the top summary block's running totals recomputed (155→216 implemented, 779→718 remaining, 384→323 pending sub-tiers [306 Bucket 2-4 + 17 M19c-i]), reconciled exactly: 216 + 323 + 1 deferred + 213 excluded + 181 residual = 934. `docs/decisions.md` new `[M19-bucket1]` entry added with full Step 0 citations. - M19-secondary-stat-on-hit (Bucket 4's single highest-leverage sub-group — unlocks all 79 `EFFECT_HIT` + stat-token moves flagged by `[M19-bucket2]`): **COMPLETE** — 2026-07-09. Step 0 re-verified everything from scratch (a genuinely different extraction method than whatever produced the original 79-list) rather than trusting `[M19-bucket2]`'s numbers blindly: 92 `EFFECT_HIT`+`MOVE_EFFECT_STAT_PLUS/MINUS` entries found, 10 genuinely multi-stat (Bucket 3, excluded — including Clangorous Soulblaze, a Z-move-exclusive whose auto-incremented enum value never resolves a numeric ID), minus Triple Arrows(771)/Make It Rain(802) (separate mechanisms) = 79, cross-checked byte-for-byte against a raw pre-compaction extraction with zero ID differences. **Count correction: the true, final figure is 79, not 78** — Bleakwind Storm(774) is confirmed double-blocked (carries BOTH the still-unbuilt weather-conditional-accuracy mechanism AND a stat-change token) but was ALREADY excluded from the 79 before this session started, so "79 minus Bleakwind Storm = 78" double-subtracts something never counted; both independent derivations agree on 79 with Bleakwind Storm already outside it. A first-draft extraction script bug was caught and fixed before generating any data: it resolved GEN-conditional ternaries by blindly taking the first branch regardless of comparison operator, misclassifying Crunch/Acid (whose two candidate sub-fields are gated by OPPOSITE-direction comparisons on the same condition) as multi-stat — fixed by resolving each ternary against its actual operator. Self-targeted fraction confirmed much higher than assumed (24/79, 30%, not "almost certainly foe-only") — the existing `stat_change_self` field already generalized correctly. Magnitude spread confirmed NOT uniform ±1 (10 moves are ±2). Guaranteed-vs-explicit-100 chance distinction confirmed to have real behavioral consequences: 10 moves (all self-targeted post-hit drops — Overheat, Draco Meteor, Leaf Storm, Psycho Boost, Fleur Cannon, Ice Hammer, Clanging Scales, Zippy Zap, Spin Out, Hammer Arm) omit `.chance` in source entirely and are encoded `secondary_chance=0` (guaranteed, Sheer-Force-exempt), matching real game behavior, vs. 69 with an explicit value remaining subject to Shield Dust/Covert Cloak/Sheer Force/Serene Grace normally. Design: `StatusManager.try_secondary_effect` gained one new escape hatch (`secondary_effect == SE_NONE and stat_change_stat >= 0 → return true`, same "caller applies it" shape as the pre-existing `SE_FLINCH` case) reusing its existing chance-roll/Serene-Grace/Shield-Dust/Covert-Cloak/Sheer-Force gating for free; its own internal early-return and `battle_manager.gd`'s caller-side gate BOTH needed widening, since these moves have `secondary_effect == SE_NONE` by construction. New `BattleManager._apply_stat_change_effect(attacker, defender, move, ng_active)` — extracted verbatim from the pre-existing pure-status-move `EFFECT_STAT_CHANGE` dispatch (Mirror Armor redirect / Defiant-Competitive / Opportunist / Mirror Herb) so the new damage-move call site reuses it exactly rather than re-deriving any of it; the pure-status-move branch now just calls this function, confirmed behavior-unchanged via regression. New dedicated `elif` branch in `_do_damaging_hit`'s `if effect_hit:` dispatch, same reasoning as the pre-existing `SE_WRAP` carve-out (the general `else` branch's status-cure-berry checks don't apply to a stat change). New `m19_secondary_stat_test.gd`/`.tscn`: one table-driven loop over all 79 moves (core data + every flag, `secondary_effect` confirmed to stay `SE_NONE`) plus 8 functional checks (±1/±2 magnitude, self-vs-foe targeting, the force_secondary=true/false gate — reusing this project's established direct-`try_secondary_effect`-call convention since no full-battle forcing seam exists for the secondary-chance roll specifically — the Sheer-Force-suppresses-and-boosts/guaranteed-chance-exempt pair, and the Mirror-Armor-redirects/self-targeted-bypasses-Mirror-Armor pair reusing `[M17n-11]`'s own full-battle pattern): 1754/1754 assertions, passed clean on the first run. Regression: `item_registry_test.tscn` 309/309, `status_test.tscn` 78/78, `stat_test.tscn` 78/78, `damage_test.tscn` 24/24 (the task's own non-negotiable set) plus a wider safety sweep given how central the extracted function is — `m17b_test.tscn` 109/109 (Defiant/Competitive), `m17n8_test.tscn` 58/58 (Opportunist), `m17n11_test.tscn` 51/51 (Mirror Armor), `m18m_test.tscn` 27/27 (Mirror Herb), `move_test.tscn` 49/49, `tier4_test.tscn` 86/86 — all unchanged. **Total move-implementation count: 351→430.** `docs/m19_subtier_plan.md` updated: Bucket 4 recomputed (141→62 moves, 28→27 sub-groups), the `M19-weather-conditional-accuracy` sub-group's description corrected to flag Bleakwind Storm's double-block explicitly, both "recommended execution order" lists updated, top summary table and reconciliation formula recomputed (430+109+1+213+181=934, reconfirmed). `docs/decisions.md` new `[M19-secondary-stat-on-hit]` entry added with full Step 0 citations, including the 78-vs-79 count correction. Next recommended tier: Bucket 3 (30 moves, still open) or any of Bucket 4's remaining 27 sub-groups, per Rob's preference.

- Bucket 3 clusters 1-2 (Thunder Fang, Ice Fang, Fire Fang, Glitzy Glow, Baddy Bad): **COMPLETE** — 2026-07-09. Closes out Bucket 3 entirely (30/30). Two independent Step 0 investigations, one per cluster, per the task's explicit instruction. **Cluster 1 (combined secondary effects)**: confirmed from source (`Cmd_setadditionaleffects`'s loop, `CalcSecondaryEffectChance`/`MoveIsAffectedBySheerForce` both keyed per-additionalEffect) that Thunder/Ice/Fire Fang's status roll and flinch roll are genuinely TWO INDEPENDENT rolls — own RNG index, own Serene-Grace doubling, own Shield-Dust/Covert-Cloak/Sheer-Force gate each — confirming the historical "10%/10%, independently rolled" framing rather than assuming it. New `secondary_effect_2`/`secondary_chance_2` fields on `MoveData` (status stays in the existing slot 1; flinch moves to the new slot 2), dispatched via a SECOND `try_secondary_effect` call on a shallow-duplicated `MoveData` — the same "duplicate and substitute" pattern `[M17n-6]` established for move-type mutation, reused here instead of changing that function's own signature, composing every existing gate correctly for free. **A real cross-tier gap found and fixed**: `[M18k]`'s King's Rock/Razor Fang mutual-exclusion gate only ever checked slot 1 for native `SE_FLINCH` — latent until this tier, since no prior move had native flinch anywhere but slot 1 — extended to check both slots, verified via a dedicated n=300 statistical rate test (King's Rock's own roll forced true) confirming the observed flinch rate tracks Thunder Fang's native ~10%, not the ~100% a stacked independent roll would produce if the fix were absent. **Cluster 2 (screen+damage)**: confirmed both Glitzy Glow/Baddy Bad are `EFFECT_HIT` (power 80/accuracy 95 at GEN_LATEST) with a guaranteed (no `.chance` field), self-targeted `MOVE_EFFECT_LIGHT_SCREEN`/`MOVE_EFFECT_REFLECT` additional effect, dispatched via the SAME `TrySetReflect`/`TrySetLightScreen` source calls the pure-status Reflect/Light Screen moves already use — confirmed, by actually tracing it rather than assuming either way, that this project's own `is_reflect`/`is_light_screen` dispatch branches return immediately with zero damage dealt, meaning a damaging move genuinely could NOT reach them before this tier — a real gap, not a "verify it's already fine" outcome. New `sets_reflect_on_hit`/`sets_light_screen_on_hit` per-move flags, dispatched inside `_do_damaging_hit` unconditional on `damage > 0` alone (not routed through `try_secondary_effect`, since this is a guaranteed/primary effect), reusing the exact same already-up no-refresh check and Light-Clay-aware duration extension. New `m19_bucket3_cluster12_test.gd`/`.tscn`: data integrity for all 5 moves plus 11 functional checks (Cluster 1: slot 1/slot 2 direct-call firing, cross-slot independence, Sheer Force suppressing both, Shield Dust blocking both, a full-battle synthetic-100%-move integration test proving the REAL dispatch fires both effects together, the King's Rock statistical mutual-exclusion test; Cluster 2: damage+screen together for both moves, a side-index check confirming the screen always lands on side 0 — the attacker's own side, never the target's, and an already-up no-refresh test). 47/47 assertions pass, stable across 3 reruns. - Bucket 4 cheapest singles (Rage, Clear Smog, Incinerate, Sparkling Aria, Throat Chop, Eerie Spell, Blood Moon — 7 of 9 originally-proposed single-move sub-groups): **COMPLETE** — 2026-07-09. Secret Power(290) and Uproar(253), the other 2 moves in this batch, were investigated with the same Step 0 rigor but explicitly DEFERRED by Rob via `AskUserQuestion`, not shipped. **Secret Power**: its secondary depends on `gBattleEnvironment`, an overworld map/tile-derived field this project has zero analog for (no map system at all) — confirmed `BATTLE_ENVIRONMENT_PLAIN`'s own GEN_LATEST effect is a trivial 30% Paralysis chance (fully schema-representable, offered as the cheap option), but Rob chose to defer entirely rather than hardcode. **Uproar**: turned out to need the SAME multi-turn forced-move-repeat primitive (`gLockedMoves`) Bucket 4's still-unbuilt `M19-rampage` sub-group (Thrash/Petal Dance/Outrage/Raging Fury) needs — genuinely not "cheap/self-contained" like this session's other 8 moves — plus a field-wide (BOTH sides, a real correction to a plausible "self-team-only" assumption) sleep-infliction block and a one-time wake-everyone-up trigger; Rob chose to defer and bundle with a future M19-rampage tier rather than build the shared lock now. Of the 7 shipped: **Rage** confirmed NOT a rampage-lock either (no `gLockedMoves` in its own case) — a simple `rage_active` volatile set on a successful hit, cleared when a different move is chosen, whose reactive half raises the holder's own Attack +1 on any subsequent damaging hit taken (self/ally-hit excluded). **Clear Smog** resets all 7 stat stages to exactly 0 (an absolute reset the existing relative-delta schema can't represent — no Haze precedent exists to reuse, since Haze itself remains unimplemented). **Incinerate** destroys (not consumes) the target's held Berry, deliberately bypassing this project's `_consume_item` (which would incorrectly also trigger Cheek Pouch/register `last_consumed_berry`) while still correctly triggering Unburden via a small dedicated destroy-path; Gems are permanently moot (none exist in this project). **Sparkling Aria** cures the TARGET's own burn, the inverse of every existing self-cure precedent. **Throat Chop** and **Eerie Spell** are both explicit chance=100 true secondaries needing their own new `SE_THROAT_CHOP`/`SE_EERIE_SPELL` constants; Eerie Spell resolved the task's own "does per-Pokémon last-move tracking exist" question with a clean yes — this project's pre-existing `last_move_used` field (wired since `[M16e]`'s Conversion 2) already answers it, zero new state needed. **Blood Moon** reuses that SAME `last_move_used` field for its own "can't use twice in a row" check (reference-equality, the same pattern the existing Disable check uses) — resolving the task's own "can these two share one mechanism" question with an even cheaper answer than proposed: reuse an existing field, not build a new shared one. New `MoveData` fields (`is_rage`/`is_clear_smog`/`is_incinerate`/`is_sparkling_aria`/`cant_use_twice`, plus the two new `SE_*` constants), new `BattlePokemon.rage_active`/`throat_chop_turns` volatiles (both switch-cleared), new `status_cured` signal. New `m19_bucket4_cheap_singles_test.gd`/`.tscn`: 46/46 assertions, stable across 4 reruns. **A real self-inflicted bug was found and fixed mid-session**: an earlier `Edit` call in this SAME session (adding `rage_active`/`throat_chop_turns` to `battle_pokemon.gd`) had accidentally deleted the pre-existing `last_consumed_berry` field declaration instead of preserving it alongside the new fields — silently breaking `_consume_item`'s Harvest/Cud-Chew tracker assignment, surfaced by this tier's own Sticky Hold discriminator test crashing with a spurious type-mismatch error. - M19-steal-stats / M19-ally-targeting-stat-change (Spectral Thief, Howl, Aromatic Mist, Coaching — 4 moves, 2 sub-groups): **COMPLETE** — 2026-07-09. Closes Bucket 4's last two "cleanly buildable" sub-groups (per the task's own Step 2 classification), leaving only gated/deferred sub-groups behind. Fixed in the docs, not further root-caused. Step 2 found BOTH sub-groups' own plan-doc notes were wrong, exactly as the task's own prompt anticipated: `M19-steal-stats`'s "reuse Opportunist's pattern" note was wrong — Opportunist reacts to a fresh stat-RISE EVENT elsewhere without touching the original mon's own stage; Spectral Thief instead snapshots-and-TRANSFERS whatever positive stages already exist across ALL 7 stats (confirmed via source's `NUM_BATTLE_STATS = NUM_STATS + 2`, wider than Starf Berry's own 5-stat pool), zeroing the target's stage in the process, dispatched via `.preAttackEffect = TRUE` (fires before the move's own accuracy roll, confirmed via a forced-miss test that the steal still fires) — a genuinely new orchestration was built instead, reusing only `StatusManager.apply_stat_change` as the mutation primitive. `M19-ally-targeting-stat-change`'s "no ally-targeting mechanism exists in any form" claim was also wrong — Helping Hand (`[M14b]`) already provides exactly this shape (`TARGET_ALLY`, fails if not doubles), and its own implementation never relies on the pre-resolved `defender` variable at all, instead computing the ally directly via the pre-existing `BattleManager._get_ally()` — meaning zero changes to move-selection/targeting AI were needed anywhere. Howl (`TARGET_USER_AND_ALLY` at GEN_LATEST) bolts the self-buff's own stat change onto the user's ally too (new `also_boosts_ally` flag, a no-op in singles); Aromatic Mist/Coaching (both genuinely `TARGET_ALLY`, never self) reuse `_apply_stat_change_effect` directly with the ally passed in place of `defender`, dispatched before the foe-targeting/Substitute/type-immunity block since none of that applies to an ally move; Coaching's 2-stat payload reuses the pre-existing `extra_stat_change_stats`/`amounts` mechanism (`[Bucket 3 multi-stat]`) with zero further changes. Spectral Thief's per-stat +6 cap gate was confirmed via direct source read (`battle_script_commands.c` L3355) to cover BOTH halves of the transfer together — when the attacker is already capped on a stat, the defender's matching stage is left untouched too, not zeroed anyway — caught as a real test-authoring bug during this session's own test-writing and fixed by re-reading source rather than trusting the initial assumption. Two real test-authoring bugs fixed on the first run, both fresh recurrences of CLAUDE.md's own documented "type-immunity-precedes-ability-logic" pitfall: the initial Spectral Thief fixtures used a Normal-type defender against the Ghost-type attacker in every positive-case test, a flat 0× immunity silently blocking the steal in every scenario — fixed by switching to a neutral Water-type defender and keeping Normal-type only for the dedicated immunity-discriminator test (whose own assertion was also corrected — this project's general damaging-move path has no distinct "immune" signal for an ordinary 0× hit, it just flows through as `move_executed` with `amount=0`). New `MoveData` fields: `steals_positive_stat_stages`, `stat_change_target_ally`, `also_boosts_ally`. New `m19_bucket4_final_pairs_test.gd`/`.tscn`: 27/27 assertions, passing after the two fixture fixes above. Regression: the 4 required suites plus `doubles_test` (54/54, `_get_ally`/doubles dispatch touched), `m17n8_test` (58/58, Opportunist's own origin suite, confirming the corrected understanding didn't disturb it), `m17l_test` (45/45, Helping Hand's doubles-redirect neighborhood), `m19_secondary_stat_test` (1754/1754) and `m19_bucket3_multistat_test` (366/366, both reuse `_apply_stat_change_effect`) — all unchanged, 0 failures. **Total move-implementation count: 513→517.** `docs/m19_subtier_plan.md` updated throughout: the 6→5 doc-drift fixed, both sub-groups marked CLOSED/COMPLETE, Bucket 4's own total shrunk 9→5 moves/6→3 sub-groups, Section A's Tier 4 row updated (80→84 implemented, 232→228 remaining, attributed to Tier 4 as a disclosed simplification matching `[Bucket 4 2-move sub-groups]`'s own precedent), Section E and top summary reconciled together (517+22+1+213+181=934, reconfirmed). `docs/decisions.md` new `[M19-steal-stats] / [M19-ally-targeting-stat-change]` entry added with full Step 0/2 citations. **Bucket 4's final state: 5 moves across 3 named sub-groups, all gated or deferred** — `M19-secret-power` (1 move, Secret Power(290), deferred by Rob pending an overworld-terrain scope call), `M19-trap-secondary` (1 move, Spirit Shackle(625), gated on M19f), `M19-blocked-on-other-tier4` (3 moves, Sappy Seed(685)/Freezy Frost(686)/Sparkly Swirl(687), gated on Leech Seed(73)/Haze(114)/Aromatherapy-or-Heal-Bell — re-confirmed all 3 still genuinely unbuilt via direct grep before closing this session). - M19e / M19f (Morning Sun, Synthesis, Moonlight, Shore Up, Spider Web, Mean Look, Block, Spirit Shackle, Jaw Lock — 9 moves, 2 sub-tiers): **COMPLETE** — 2026-07-09. Two further nuances: Strong Winds is treated as "no weather" (not "other weather") for the 3 sun-based moves specifically; Utility Umbrella strips SUN/RAIN only (not sand/hail) for those same 3 moves and has zero effect on Shore Up at all. **M19f Step 0**: confirmed Spider Web/Mean Look/Block (`EFFECT_MEAN_LOOK`) and Spirit Shackle's own secondary (`MOVE_EFFECT_PREVENT_ESCAPE`) dispatch through the literal same underlying state (`volatiles.escapePrevention`/`battlerPreventingEscape`) — genuinely the same mechanism, not just thematically similar. `AbilityManager.is_trapped()`'s own pre-existing doc comment (written back at `[M17f]`) had already anticipated this exact move-based trap by name, so extending it needed only a 1-line addition mirroring `wrapped_by`'s shape exactly. Shed Shell's exemption needed ZERO new code — already gated at the `_phase_move_selection` call site (wired during `[M18r]`), confirmed to apply uniformly to every trapping source. Two real, source-confirmed asymmetries found and correctly modeled: (1) `ignoresProtect` is NOT uniform across the 3 status moves despite sharing one effect ID (Spider Web=FALSE, Mean Look/Block=TRUE at GEN_LATEST); (2) the Ghost-type immunity Mean Look/Block/Spider Web all carry is a MOVE-SCRIPT-level check baked into their own dedicated script, absent from the generic secondary-effect dispatch Spirit Shackle uses — meaning Spirit Shackle CAN trap a Ghost-type target while the 3 status moves cannot, and — since Spider Web is Bug-type (only 0.5× vs Ghost, not a chart immunity, unlike Normal-type Mean Look/Block which the general type gate would've caught for free) — Spider Web genuinely needs its own explicit check to match source, tested as the key discriminator. Jaw Lock's `MOVE_EFFECT_TRAP_BOTH` confirmed as a genuine THIRD variant of the same mechanism: sets the same fields on BOTH battlers simultaneously, gated on an all-or-nothing guard (if either is already trapped, neither side's trap is set). - M19c / M19d (Wide Guard, Quick Guard, Spiky Shield, Baneful Bunker, Obstruct, Silk Trap, Burning Bulwark, Metal Burst, Mirror Move — 9 moves, 2 sub-tiers): **COMPLETE** — 2026-07-09. Confirmed genuinely non-uniform beyond that shared base: Obstruct/Silk Trap block only non-status moves; Wide Guard/Quick Guard are side-wide, confirmed via source's own `IsSideProtected` (reads the SAME per-battler field for either battler on the side) that this needed NO new `_side_conditions`-style infrastructure at all — just also checking the defender's ally's own `protect_active`/`protect_method`; Wide Guard blocks only spread moves (`is_spread`), Quick Guard blocks only priority>0 moves via the SAME ability-boosted priority computation `[M17k]`'s `blocks_priority_move` already built. The 5 contact-punish variants (Spiky Shield's maxHP/8 recoil, Baneful Bunker's poison, Burning Bulwark's burn, Obstruct's -2 Def, Silk Trap's -1 Speed) are gated on `AbilityManager.move_triggers_contact_retaliation` (`[M18p]`'s Protective-Pads-aware wrapper, confirmed the correct gate from source). A real correctness gap was closed proactively: Obstruct/Silk Trap's stat-drops now trigger Defiant/Competitive too, via the same reactive-check shape `_apply_one_stat_change_pair` already establishes for "an opponent lowered my stat" — tested via a dedicated discriminator. **M19d Step 0**: Metal Burst confirmed the same `EFFECT_REFLECT_DAMAGE` shape as Counter/Mirror Coat, but with THREE real asymmetries — 1.5x not 2x; reflects EITHER category (whichever was hit LAST if both landed in one turn, via a new `last_hit_was_special` flag), not one; and priority=0, not their shared -5 (found fresh at Step 0, not originally flagged) — kept as its own separate `metal_burst` flag rather than generalizing `counter`/`mirror_coat`, avoiding risk to their already-tested dispatch. **Mirror Move — the one point given real Step 0 attention, confirmed via direct source read**: `GetMirrorMoveMove` reads the move that hit the MIRROR MOVE USER itself (`lastTakenMove[gBattlerAttacker]`), NOT the target's own last-used move — a genuinely different tracking axis this project's existing `_last_attacker`/`_last_attacker_move` dictionaries (already built for Destiny Bond/Aftermath/Innards Out) already capture exactly, needing zero new tracking state. Confirmed Mirror Move dispatches through the literal same `CancelerCallSubmove` mechanism as Metronome — reused the existing "reassign `move` and fall through" pattern directly, with `defender` also reassigned to the actual hitter (`_last_attacker`) for doubles-correctness. New `BattlePokemon.protect_method`/`last_hit_was_special` fields plus 8 `PROTECT_METHOD_*` constants; new `MoveData.protect_method`/`metal_burst`/`is_mirror_move` fields; new `BattleManager._is_protected_from`/`_apply_protect_contact_punish`/`_apply_protect_stat_punish` helpers. - D1 free candidates (Solar Blade(632), Snipe Shot(691), Hidden Power(237), Hyperspace Fury(621) — 4 moves): **COMPLETE** — 2026-07-09. Step 0 re-verified each fresh rather than trusting the recon's own "free" label, per this arc's standing rule — found 2 real corrections and flagged 1 pre-existing gap. **Solar Blade**: confirmed it shares Solar Beam's own literal `EFFECT_SOLAR_BEAM` (not a separate effect) and that `is_solar_beam`'s charge-skip dispatch is category-agnostic — clean reuse. Flagged, not fixed: source's own rain/sand/hail/fog damage-halving for this effect was never built for Solar Beam(76) itself (only the charge-skip half exists), so Solar Blade ships with that same pre-existing gap rather than expanding scope to fix Solar Beam. **Snipe Shot**: confirmed it bypasses TWO separate source redirect mechanisms (Follow Me/Rage Powder's timer AND Lightning Rod/Storm Drain's ability check) via one effect-ID exclusion in source, and that this project's own `bypasses_redirection` call site already gates both together — extended with one new `move` param and a move-level `ignores_redirection` flag. **Hidden Power** — the real correction: at this project's GEN_LATEST config, power is a FLAT 60, not IV-derived at all (`B_HIDDEN_POWER_DMG >= GEN_6` makes the classic bit-parity power formula dead code) — simpler than the recon assumed. Two independent pieces; closes D2 entirely (every cross-cutting family surfaced by `[M19-section-d-cluster]`'s original sweep has now shipped). **Part A — real correction to the task's own two-way framing: genuinely THREE mechanism shapes, not two.** (1) Per-slot delayed scheduler — Future Sight/Doom Desire (share `EFFECT_FUTURE_SIGHT`) and Wish — new `BattleManager` dictionaries keyed by combatant SLOT INDEX (mirroring source's own per-slot `gBattleStruct` storage, whose own code comment flags this as a deliberate simplification). Future Sight/Doom Desire resolve 2 turns later against whoever OCCUPIES the target's slot then (confirmed via a dedicated switch-survival test: the original target switches out, the replacement takes the hit instead), no accuracy roll ever, resolution routed through the EXISTING `_do_damaging_hit` chokepoint (screens/Substitute/Sturdy-chain/times_hit/Air Balloon all apply for free). Confirmed source ALWAYS resolves fresh at that later turn, never freezing cast-time snapshots — the caster's `stat_stages` are already correctly zeroed by the pre-existing `_switch_out_clear` if it switched away in the meantime, reproducing most of source's own "caster no longer present" fallback for free; the one disclosed gap is this project doesn't additionally null a benched caster's ability/item the way source's own struct-swap does. Wish resolves 1 turn later against whoever occupies the CASTER'S OWN slot, healing `caster's own max HP / 2` — fixed at cast time, confirmed via a dedicated discriminator NOT the eventual recipient's own max HP. (2) Per-mon volatile counter — Yawn — confirmed genuinely NOT part of the scheduler family despite the shared framing: mechanically IDENTICAL to the already-shipped `disable_turns`/`encore_turns`/`throat_chop_turns` pattern, zero new switch/faint infrastructure, already correctly cleared by `_clear_volatiles`; resolution fires a completely fresh sleep-infliction attempt via the existing `try_apply_status` pipeline (all immunities re-derived at that moment). (3) Switch-in-triggered one-shot — Healing Wish/Lunar Dance — a single per-slot flag with no counter, consumed by the slot's next switch-in by any method; unlike Explosion/Self-Destruct, FAILS OUTRIGHT (no faint) if no valid switch target exists (new `has_valid_switch_target()`-gated check). **A real finding surfaced only while writing tests, not from source reading alone**: "any switch method" isn't independently testable as a scenario different from plain faint-replacement for this move family specifically — the stored effect is created BY the caster's own faint, and faint-replacement for that exact slot follows immediately and unconditionally, so no other switch method can ever reach the slot first; an initial "test via forced Roar" design was scrapped once this was traced through. Deliberately ran `cd /tmp` as a diagnostic: the shell did NOT move there — the environment silently reset the cwd to `/home/rob/GodotAsImagined` instead. Any `cd` at any point in a session targeting a path outside that boundary — not just the already-documented `reference/pokeemerald_expansion` case — lands the shell one level too high, silently, and every subsequent relative-path command (including `bash scripts/count_assertions.sh`) then fails to resolve; this happens BEFORE the script's own code ever runs, so no internal fix inside the script could ever have addressed it. Fixed `scripts/count_assertions.sh` itself to `cd` to its own project root unconditionally at the very top (was previously nested inside one branch) — real hardening, but not the fix for the relative-path-resolution failure itself. **The actual fix, now a dedicated standing-rule section in CLAUDE.md** (not just narrative here): always invoke the sweep via its full absolute path in the same command string — `bash /home/rob/GodotAsImagined/as-imagined/scripts/count_assertions.sh` — never a bare relative path, and never relying on a `cd` from a separate prior command (a `cd`-prefixed-then-relative invocation was explicitly NOT adopted as the primary rule, since it has also been observed to fail in this environment). Verified by deliberately reproducing the drift (`cd /tmp`, confirmed the reset) then dispatching a sweep using ONLY the hardened invocation with no manual `cd` — succeeded on the first attempt, matching the exact prior baseline (116 files/11847/0 failures). **One honest caveat**: a separate, still-unexplained transient sweep-dispatch failure (empty log, exit 1, no directory issue, immediate success on a bare retry) still occurred once during this same session's `[Perish Song]` sweeps, using the hardened invocation — flagged explicitly as a distinct, still-open flakiness class, not folded into "fixed." `docs/decisions.md` new `[Sweep-dispatch fix]` entry with the full diagnostic trail.

### Standing Step 0 checklist item: does this foe-targeting move's real script call `typecalc`?

Discovered independently four times before being made a standing checklist item: `[D2 batch 2]` (Foresight/Odor Sleuth), `[D4 bundle 3]` (Purify/Nightmare/Spite), `[D4 Bundle 6]` (Toxic Thread/Venom Drench), and the `[EFFECT_STAT_CHANGE audit]` that finally swept the rest of the family (16 more moves — Growl/Leer/Screech/etc.).

This project's `BattleManager._phase_move_execution` runs every foe-targeting move with a real type through one general type-immunity gate before letting the move's own effect logic run, on the assumption that real source similarly checks `typecalc` for every such move. That assumption is false for an entire family of status moves: any move whose real battle script never calls `typecalc` (confirmed so far: `BattleScript_EffectForesight`, `BattleScript_EffectStatChange` and everything that maps to it, `BattleScript_EffectReflectType`) is NEVER subject to a type-immunity check in the real engine — including against its own primary, flavor-intended use case (Nightmare vs. a sleeping Normal-type target; Toxic Thread vs. a Steel-type switch-in; a plain Normal-type stat-lowering move vs. a Ghost-type).

**Before implementing or auditing any foe-targeting status move (or move family) going forward**: read the move's real battle script directly (`data/battle_scripts_1.s`, or trace `sMoveEffectTable`/`battle_move_effects.h` to find which script the move's `.effect` maps to) and confirm whether it calls `typecalc` anywhere. If it does not, the move needs the same treatment as the precedents above — either its own dedicated `is_*` exemption (if it also needs its own dispatch branch for other reasons) or, if it's one of a family sharing a no-`typecalc` script, the shared `MoveData.stat_change_bypasses_type_gate`-style flag — checked against this project's own `TypeChart.TABLE` to confirm the exemption is actually reachable (not moot, like the 9 Memento-shaped exclusions above) before spending test-writing effort on it.

### Standing Step 0 checklist item: a new consumer of a dormant `MoveData` field needs a full-roster grep, not just the moves already in mind

A recurring gap shape across this whole M19/M21.5 arc: a `MoveData` field already exists in the schema and already has real ability/item logic reading it, but was never actually SET on every move that should carry it per source — only on the specific moves a session happened to be thinking about at the time. Confirmed instances: Ice Ball's `ballistic_move` (flagged in a comment since `[M16b]` but never actually set on the data dict until `[M17n-1]`), Air Balloon/Iron Ball's groundedness (`[M18t]`), Mega Punch/Headlong Rush's `punching_move` and Aerial Ace's `slicing_move` (M21.5 Session 3's Part 4 Punch-family check), and 69 more moves across 10 flag categories found by M21.5's own Bucket 1 full-roster sweep.

**Before building any new ability/item mechanic that reads an existing-but-previously-unconsumed `MoveData` field**: grep the full roster (`gen_moves.py`, or the reference `moves_info.h` struct field directly) for every move that should carry the flag per source — not just the specific named moves already in mind for that session. A session scoped to "does move X need this flag" will reliably miss sibling moves Y and Z that need the identical flag for the identical reason.

- Bugfix — embedded team builder rendered at zero height on `roster_screen.tscn`: **COMPLETE** — 2026-07-17. Reported by Rob from real windowed play. Root cause, confirmed via a real non-headless screenshot: `team_builder_screen.tscn`'s root `Control` is anchor-laid-out (correct for its two established top-level usages), but `roster_screen.gd` embeds it as a child of a `VBoxContainer` — in Godot 4 a `Container` always overrides a Control child's position/size via `custom_minimum_size`/`size_flags`, which the builder's root had never needed to set before, collapsing its rendered height to 0. Fixed with 2 lines in `roster_screen.gd`'s own embedding call site (`custom_minimum_size = Vector2(0, 1000)` + `size_flags_vertical = SIZE_EXPAND_FILL`) — `team_builder_screen.tscn` itself untouched, since its other 2 usages never went through a `Container` and were never affected. Confirmed via grep this is the ONLY place any screen scene is embedded as a child rather than swapped in via `change_scene_to_file` — every other M23 navigation path is categorically unaffected. Root-caused why `m23_5_team_persistence_test.gd` (which DOES exercise the exact buggy code path) never caught this: every existing assertion checked logical/state correctness only, never the resulting Control's actual rendered size — closed with a new `S2.02b` assertion, proven to actually catch the regression (reverted the fix, reran, got the expected failure; restored, reran clean). Regression: 143 files, GRAND TOTAL 13790→13791 (+1, exactly the new guard assertion), zero other differences across 2 sweeps. See `docs/m23_recon.md`'s own `## Bugfix — embedded team builder...` entry.

M23.11 is the "pull reference-material art assets into the project" sub-arc
of M23 (Simulator layer). Full session-by-session detail (Step 0 findings,
screenshot verification, regression-sweep numbers) for every phase below
lives in `docs/m23_recon.md`'s own `## M23.11` section — this table plus
the bullets right below it are the CLAUDE.md-level summary every other
milestone in this file already gets; they were simply never written for
M23.11 until this pass (found via a Phase 5 roadmap-consistency check).
Phase numbering has a genuine, pre-existing gap (2 → 4a) — not a mistake
introduced here, confirmed via direct search of `docs/m23_recon.md` itself
(no "Phase 3" was ever defined).

|---|---|---|

- M23.11 Phase 5a (battle background reconstruction + manual picker): **COMPLETE** — 2026-07-19. First real implementation session against the locked Phase 5 scope (`docs/m23_11_phase5_recon.md` Section 0). Step 0 re-derived the tile/tilemap/palette structure directly against all 11 real base tilesets, not just the single `rock` sample the original recon decoded — confirmed uniform (128×128 4bpp indexed `tiles.png`, 4096-byte/2048-entry `map.bin`, JASC-PAL `palette.pal`) with two real surprises: (1) exactly 2 distinct tilemap LAYOUTS are shared across all 11, confirmed via direct md5sum — Group A (cave/long_grass/pond_water/rock/tall_grass/underwater/water) and Group B (building/sand/sky/stadium) are each byte-identical within their group; (2) `stadium` has no own default `palette.pal` (only 8 named recolor variants) — resolved via a documented judgment call, using `battle_frontier.pal` as the least context-specific default. Screen-entry format confirmed as standard GBA BG (bits 0-9 tile index, bit 10/11 h/v-flip, bits 12-15 palette bank); the 64×32-tile canvas confirmed (via a block-major-vs-row-major visual comparison, not assumed) to be two side-by-side 32×32 screen blocks. A small fraction of entries (32/2048) reference an out-of-range palette bank, wrapped rather than left as magenta-placeholder artifacts. The composited canvas's real content sits in roughly its top 12-14 tile rows with a large flat area beneath — confirmed structurally intentional (both shared layouts independently show the same shape, matching the real GBA battle screen's own message-box-occluded lower region) rather than a decode bug, resolving the crop to exactly the top-left 240×160px (one full GBA screen). New `scripts/gen_battle_backgrounds.py` (idempotent, mirrors `gen_pokemon_sprites.py`/`gen_trainer_portraits.py`'s established shape) writes 11 flat PNGs to `assets/sprites/battle_backgrounds/`. New `BattleBackgroundRegistry` (`scripts/battle/core/battle_background_registry.gd`) mirrors `TrainerPicRegistry`'s lazy-directory-scan-and-cache convention, name-keyed (no numeric battle-environment-ID concept exists elsewhere in this project). `BattleSetupContext` gained an optional `background_id` param (default `""`, every pre-existing caller unaffected). `battle_setup_screen.gd` gained a manual picker (`BackgroundRow`/`BackgroundOptionButton`, populated from the registry's own scan, not a hardcoded 11-name list) — not tied to any overworld/terrain concept, per the locked scope decision. `battle_screen.tscn` gained a `Background` `TextureRect` as the first child of `BattleStage` (so every sprite/health-box/etc. added after it draws on top for free, no `z_index` needed); `battle_screen.gd`'s `_ready()` applies the hand-off id, falling back to `"building"` (matching both source's own real `LoadBattleEnvironmentGfx` fallback and the picker's own alphabetically-first default) for every direct/`--autoplay` launch that never goes through the setup screen at all. Real screenshot verification (5 of 11 backgrounds — rock, water, tall_grass, sky, cave — exceeding the required 3): all rendered correctly and distinctly behind the existing sprite/health-box/menu layer with zero overlap or reconstruction artifacts, via a disposable `_scratch_screenshot_5a.gd`/`.tscn` driver (deleted after the session, matching the established scratch-driver precedent). New `battle_background_smoke_test.gd`/`.tscn`: 41/41, mirroring `battle_ui_sprite_smoke_test.gd`'s directory-scan precedent plus a direct exercise of the registry's own API and an exact-11-id check (unlike the UI sprite pull, this asset set has a known fixed target count). - M23.11 Phase 5b (hit-effect asset pull — hybrid model: generic library + 3 bespoke moves): **COMPLETE** — 2026-07-19. Asset staging only, per locked scope — no dispatch/UI wiring (that's 5c). This script deliberately deviates from every prior `gen_*_sprites.py`'s pure `shutil.copyfile` convention and explicitly tags index 0 transparent on every pulled sprite. **Part A**: curated 21 sprites (18 one-per-type-family + 3 non-type generic — physical impact/status puff/stat shimmer), each pick's reasoning documented inline in the new `scripts/gen_hit_effect_sprites.py`, written to `assets/sprites/battle_effects/generic/`. **Part B**, traced directly from each move's own `gBattleAnimMove_*` script in `data/battle_anim_scripts.s`, confirmed NOT uniform: Flamethrower (move 53) is a simple flat sprite pull (`small_ember.png`, self-contained). Visual inspection of both renders found clean, immediately-recognizable curling-wave compositions with **no artifacts, notably cleaner than Phase 5a's own environment-tileset output** (plausibly because this asset's whole canvas is genuinely meant to be visible, unlike Phase 5a's UI-occluded lower region).
