- M23.11 Phase 5c (hit-effect dispatch engine — hybrid model wired into `battle_screen.gd`): **COMPLETE** — 2026-07-19. First real UI-consumption session in Phase 5 — everything before this was asset staging only. Step 0 re-verified 5b's own output directly against disk rather than trusting that session's report: confirmed all 21 generic sprites + 3 bespoke moves' files, and found one thing 5b's own framing slightly overstated — `lightning.png`/`lightning_2.png` (Thunder) already carry byte-identical embedded 16-color palettes (direct PIL comparison), so no runtime pixel/palette recoloring is actually needed; `lightning_2.png` is used as a genuine second visual layer (a short follow-up flash played immediately after the main bolt) instead. New `scripts/battle/core/hit_effect_registry.gd` (`class_name HitEffectRegistry`, `RefCounted`, mirrors `BattleBackgroundRegistry`'s static-loader convention) is the pure "which texture(s)" lookup: `move_id_of()` recovers a move's numeric id from its own `.resource_path` (`MoveData` has no id field of its own — `move_registry.gd`'s own doc comment already establishes id-via-filename-convention only) rather than matching on `move_name` text; a special-case branch checks Flamethrower(53)/Thunder(87)/Surf(57) first, falling through to a generic `move.type`/`move.category` dispatch otherwise. A real design bug was caught and fixed before it shipped: checking `move.type` before `move.category` would have made `stat_shimmer`/`status_puff` almost unreachable, since nearly every status move still carries a real elemental `.type` (Growl/Swords Dance are `TYPE_NORMAL`, Toxic is `TYPE_POISON`, etc.) — category now gates first for STATUS-category moves, type only drives the sprite pick for damaging moves. `compute_frame_layout()` is a pure square-sub-frame-stripping function (frame size = min dimension, count = major/minor when evenly divisible) with an explicit non-cropping fallback for `steel.png`'s own irregular 16×40 shape (5b's own "flagged not fixed" case). Rendering lives in `battle_screen.gd` itself (matching how `_apply_background()` consumes `BattleBackgroundRegistry`): one shared `_play_multi_stage_strip_effect()` Tween-driven renderer covers the generic library, Flamethrower, AND Thunder's two-stage playback (spawns a `TextureRect`+`AtlasTexture` at the target's `get_global_rect().get_center()`, steps through each texture's own frame count via `tween_callback`, holds, fades, frees) — confirmed via direct recon re-read that only Surf genuinely needs a different rendering path (a `clip_contents` `Control` window with the full uncropped 512×256 BG canvas panning horizontally underneath it, "a brief scrolling pan," per the locked framing) rather than assuming all 3 bespoke moves are interchangeable. New `EffectLayer` `Control` node, the LAST child of `BattleStage` in `battle_screen.tscn` (draws on top of every sprite/health-box for free, no `z_index` needed, while still sitting underneath `VBox`'s message-box/menu since that's a later sibling at the `BattleScreen` root — zero risk of an effect visually covering the log or menu). Targeting: `_sprite_node_for()`/`_field_slot_for()` reuse Phase 4d's own party/`active_indices`/slot model with zero new `BattleManager`-side concept — confirmed correct in both singles and doubles via real screenshots (a doubles Flamethrower aimed at the opponent's slot 1 rendered at slot 1, not slot 0; a doubles Surf — a real spread/`TARGET_BOTH` move — independently spawned its own wave effect at EACH opponent slot, since `move_executed` already fires once per target). Timing/sequencing: wired as a completely separate `move_executed.connect()` alongside the pre-existing log handler (Godot signals support multiple independent listeners) — no `await` anywhere in the new code, so an effect's Tween runs fully independently of turn/message sequencing. A real bug surfaced only under `--autoplay`'s own immediate `get_tree().quit()` (never during normal interactive play): a still-animating effect's Tween could be mid-flight when the battle ended, leaking `ObjectDB` instances at process exit (confirmed via a direct git-stash A/B comparison that this was genuinely new, not pre-existing) — fixed with a small `_active_hit_effect_nodes` tracking array + `_clear_active_hit_effects()` called from `_on_battle_ended`, which kills each effect's own Tween (stored via `set_meta()`) BEFORE freeing its node (freeing first, tried initially, left a queued `tween_callback` step erroring against an already-freed node next frame — a second real bug this same verification pass caught). Real, non-headless screenshot verification (8 scenarios, exceeding the required minimum of 3 bespoke + 3 generic): Flamethrower, Thunder (needed a retry — its own real ~70% accuracy missed on the first roll, correctly producing NO effect, confirming the dispatcher correctly does nothing on a miss), Surf, Tackle (physical/Normal), Psychic (special), Swords Dance (status, self-target) in singles, plus a doubles Surf (both opponent slots) and a doubles Flamethrower (opponent slot 1 specifically) — all via a disposable `_scratch_screenshot_5c.gd`/`.tscn` driver (deleted after the session, same precedent as Phase 5a's own scratch driver), driving `battle_screen.tscn` directly (non-headless — real windowed rendering was required, since `--headless` mode's dummy renderer does not actually rasterize anything meaningful to screenshot). This pass caught ONE further real visual bug beyond the two above: Surf's clip window was initially vertically CENTERED on the 512×256 canvas, landing on a large flat-blue band and rendering as a featureless blue rectangle instead of the actual curling wave — fixed by discovering (via direct visual inspection of both pulled source images, not assumed) that the two variants are MIRRORED, not identically laid out: `water_player.png`'s wave crest sits at the TOP of its canvas, `water_opponent.png`'s sits at the BOTTOM (thematically sensible — each side's own wave crests away from its own side of the screen) — the vertical anchor now follows `attacker_is_player` instead of using one fixed offset for both. New `scenes/battle/hit_effect_dispatch_test.gd`/`.tscn`: 40/40, covering `HitEffectRegistry`'s pure lookup logic (id resolution, bespoke detection, the type-vs-category dispatch priority bug above as a named regression guard, frame-layout math including the irregular-source fallback) plus `_sprite_node_for`/`_field_slot_for` in both singles and doubles via a bare `BattleScreen.new()` + plain unattached nodes, mirroring `phase4d_doubles_visual_test.gd`'s own established pattern (the actual Tween/node-creation code needs a live `SceneTree` for `create_tween()`, so that part is covered by the real screenshot pass instead, not a unit test). Also caught and fixed mid-session: an unrelated `cwd`-drift footgun (a stray `cd` inside a Python one-liner silently reset the shell's working directory to the outer repo root for several subsequent commands, making Godot invocations point at an invalid project path and hang indefinitely) — CLAUDE.md's own "known footgun" section already warned about exactly this class of bug. Regression: before baseline confirmed fresh at 158 files/23,442 (re-run directly this session, matching 5b's own recorded total exactly) → two after-sweeps, **159 files / GRAND TOTAL 23,482** and 23,481 — the 1-assertion difference isolated via 3 direct `m24c_test.tscn` reruns (28/28, 27/28, 27/28) to the same already-documented pre-existing flake 5b itself called out, 0 real regressions. Phase 5a's background art/reconstruction script were NOT touched this session, per the explicit standing deferral. Palette-only recolors (5d) remain untouched and still deferred.

- M25a (battle-engine correctness bugs found during a real playthrough): **COMPLETE** — 2026-07-19. Four bugs from CLAUDE.md's own M25a roadmap scope note, each investigated via direct Step 0 reproduction before any fix, per this project's own standing discipline. **Bug 1 (shared-HP-pool hardlock on a spread move)**: the bug report's own hypothesis (`PokemonFactory`/species-construction caching returning a shared object for two same-species party slots) was directly disproved via a repro (`g1 != g2`, independently-constructed every time) — the real root cause, found via a 60-random-doubles-battle stress test, was FOUR distinct aliasing/hardlock bugs, none related to construction at all: (1) `BattleManager._get_replacement_slot` (normal `SWITCH_PROMPT` faint replacement) was missing the exact `not party.active_indices.has(slot)` guard its sibling `_get_baton_pass_slot` already carried, letting a human player's own queued replacement alias two fainted doubles field slots onto the same party member; (2) the same function also needed to exclude a doubles sibling combatant's own pending-but-not-yet-applied voluntary switch (`_chosen_switch_slots`, decided in `MOVE_SELECTION` but not applied until that combatant's own later `ACTION_EXECUTION` turn) — a race window plain `active_indices` can't see; (3) `TrainerAI.choose_action_doubles`' SMART-tier proactive-switch check could let two ALLIED combatants both pick the identical bench slot in one turn (fixed by threading the ally's own already-chosen slot through as a new `ally_chosen_switch_slot`/`excluded_slot` parameter chain), and its own `_best_switch_target` had a second, sharper bug — when the excluded slot was the ONLY live non-active candidate, its fallback (`BattleParty.get_first_non_fainted_not_active()`, no exclusion parameter) picked the excluded slot right back up anyway, confirmed via direct trace as the exact mechanism behind a residual ~1.7% collision rate the other three fixes alone didn't close; (4) the REAL `battle_screen.gd` UI, when a forced replacement (`SWITCH_PROMPT`) had genuinely zero valid bench candidates, rendered ZERO buttons and no "Back" button either — a real hardlock (BattleManager waits indefinitely for `queue_replacement_for()` on a human-controlled side, and nothing could ever call it) — plausibly the single most direct match for "hard-locks the game" as actually experienced in real play; fixed by extracting a new pure `BattleScreen._party_has_switch_candidate()` helper and auto-submitting an explicit "no replacement" (-1) + `advance()` when it's false. Verified via a disposable stress-test driver (not committed): 180 random doubles battles across 3 RNG seeds, 0 hangs / 0 aliasing after all four fixes (before: up to 40/60 hangs and 21/60 aliasing on a single seed). **Bug 2 (in doubles, a mid-turn KO skips the second Pokémon's own turn)**: root-caused directly — `_phase_faint_check` correctly routes any mid-turn faint to `SWITCH_PROMPT`, but `_phase_switch_prompt`'s own ending UNCONDITIONALLY jumped to `BATTLE_END_CHECK` → (battle not over) a fresh `MOVE_SELECTION`, silently dropping every other not-yet-acted combatant's own already-queued action for the CURRENT turn — invisible in singles (a faint there always coincides with the turn's action queue already being exhausted) but a real, reproducible bug in doubles, confirmed via a direct fixture (`current_actor_index` only reached 1 of 4 after the first KO, the player's own second Pokémon and both remaining opponents never acting). Fixed by mirroring `_phase_faint_check`'s own already-correct `_current_actor_index < _turn_order.size()` check at `_phase_switch_prompt`'s ending — resumes `ACTION_EXECUTION` when the current turn still has combatants pending AND neither side has been fully defeated (added specifically so a mid-turn full-side wipe still ends the battle immediately rather than resuming the winning side's remaining actions, matching the real games); every other case (an end-of-turn-triggered faint, or the faint being the LAST action's own faint) falls through to the exact same `BATTLE_END_CHECK` path as before, a pure additive change. **Bug 3 (opponent's "entry animation" repeats instead of playing once)**: investigated, initially concluded NOT a bug — direct inspection of both `battle_screen.tscn` (`OpponentAnimTimer`: `wait_time=0.5`, `autostart=true`, Godot's own `one_shot` default is `false`) and `_on_opponent_anim_timer_timeout()`'s own extensive Phase 4c doc comments found the continuous alternation deliberately designed as an ambient idle-bob ("the Pokémon is alive" indicator), not a misfiring one-shot; no code changed this session. **[Corrected in M25b, same day]**: that conclusion trusted Phase 4c's own prior characterization instead of checking it against the actual reference source, which is exactly what this project's own Step 0 discipline exists to prevent. A follow-up check of `pokeemerald_expansion/src/sprite.c`'s real `AnimCmd` interpreter found it sets `animEnded = TRUE` and stops (no jump back to frame 0) once a species' own `frontAnimFrames` sequence hits its `ANIMCMD_END`, and `pokemon.c`'s `DoMonFrontSpriteAnimation` triggers it once, on the Pokémon's own appearance — the real games play this as a brief ONE-SHOT double-bob, not a forever-looping ambient indicator. See M25b's own entry below for the actual fix. **Bug 4 (no Struggle when out of PP)**: Struggle itself was already fully implemented at the engine level (`_struggle_move`/`_is_forced_struggle`, wired into the AI-controlled and default-fallback branches of `_phase_move_selection` since an earlier milestone) — NOT genuinely unbuilt, confirmed via direct search before assuming absence. The real, narrower gap: the human-controlled branch's own `elif _human_controlled[side]: continue` fired unconditionally regardless of PP state, permanently stalling `MOVE_SELECTION` for a human player out of PP everywhere — and even without the stall, `battle_screen.gd`'s own move-selection menu (`_build_main_menu`) had no path to ever submit a "Struggle" action at all, since Struggle isn't a member of `mon.moves` and `queue_move_targeted()`'s own `mon.moves[idx]` lookup can never resolve it. Fixed in three parts: the human-controlled branch's own condition now excludes the forced-Struggle case, with a new sibling branch auto-assigning `_struggle_move` directly (matching how AI/default-fallback combatants already worked — the real games don't even show a Fight menu when Struggle is forced); a new public `BattleManager.is_forced_struggle()` wrapper (battle_screen.gd stays on the public API surface, per this project's own convention); and `_current_action_field_slot()` now recognizes an already-auto-resolved forced-Struggle slot the same way it already recognizes a fainted one, so the UI doesn't render a stale, all-disabled-buttons Fight menu for it. New test suites: `m25a_switch_aliasing_test.gd`/`.tscn` (17/17, Bug 1's four sub-fixes plus the original construction-identity hypothesis explicitly disproven as its own assertion), `m25a_doubles_midturn_faint_test.gd`/`.tscn` (7/7, Bug 2's fix plus two non-regression cases — last-actor faint, full-side wipe), `m25a_struggle_test.gd`/`.tscn` (10/10, Bug 4's fix plus a no-regression case for a human side that still has real PP). Regression: two full sweeps after all four fixes landed, **162 files / GRAND TOTAL 23,516** and 23,515 — exactly Phase 5c's own closing baseline (159/23,482 and 159/23,481) plus this session's 34 new assertions (17+7+10) and 3 new files, the familiar 1-assertion `m24c_test.tscn` flake accounting for the rest, 0 real regressions. Bug 2's fix (the deepest, touching core phase-transition logic) was verified with a dedicated full sweep on its own before Bugs 3/4 were even started, given its own risk profile. Real screenshot/playthrough-style verification was judged unnecessary beyond the direct `BattleManager`-level fixture proof already obtained (HP deltas conclusively show both the previously-skipped combatant and its target took real damage) — Bug 3's own conclusion (later corrected same-day, see above) needed no code change at the time. M25c-h remain unscoped-for-implementation, per M25's own locked roadmap-row sequencing; M25b (menu restructuring + Bug 3's real fix) landed the same day — see its own entry immediately below.

- M25b (core battle menu — Fight/Item/Switch/Run — plus the Bug 3 idle-animation fix): **COMPLETE** — 2026-07-19. Step 0 traced the existing button-list implementation directly: `battle_screen.gd`'s old `_build_main_menu()` rendered every move button INLINE alongside Switch/Item (no real top-level tier at all — moves, Switch, and Item all lived on one flat screen), while `Menu.SWITCH`/`Menu.ITEM`/`Menu.TARGET_SELECT` were already real, working sub-menu states with their own "Back" buttons returning to `Menu.MAIN`. **Menu redesign**: `enum Menu` gained a real two-tier shape — `TOP` (renamed from `MAIN`) now shows exactly Fight/Switch/Item/Run; picking Fight enters a NEW `FIGHT` state showing the old inline move-button loop (content unchanged, just moved one tier deeper), with its own "Back" returning to `TOP`. `_build_main_menu()` was split into `_build_top_menu()` (the 4 new top-level buttons) and `_build_fight_menu()` (the moved move-list + its own Back). Every existing "Back → `Menu.MAIN`" site was renamed to `Menu.TOP`, with ONE deliberate exception: `TARGET_SELECT`'s own "Back" now returns to `FIGHT` (the immediate previous step, not all the way back to TOP) — so picking a different move doesn't require re-navigating through the top menu. **Run**: a temporary placeholder per this sub-phase's own locked scope (no real flee logic — success chance/speed/trainer-refusal are explicitly out of scope) — `_on_run_pressed()` mirrors `_on_play_again_pressed()`'s own exact shape (a bare `change_scene_to_file()` to `battle_setup_screen.tscn`), plus an explicit `_clear_active_hit_effects()` call first (matching the exact Tween-leak fix M25c's own session already applied to the normal win/loss path, so Run doesn't reintroduce it for the one path that doesn't go through `_on_battle_ended`). Confirmed `BattleSetupContext` needs no explicit reset — it's already cleared at CONSUMPTION time in `_ready()`, not at battle-end, so there's nothing stale for the next launch regardless of how a battle ends. **Doubles compatibility**: confirmed explicitly, not assumed — the entire menu system already threads `field_slot` through every builder via Phase 4f's own established per-slot sequential-menu pattern (one flat `_menu` variable, `_slot_acted`/`_current_action_field_slot()` tracking which slot it currently applies to), so TOP/FIGHT needed zero new doubles-specific plumbing; verified via both a direct test (slot 0 and slot 1 each get their own independently-built 4-option top menu and correctly-per-mon Fight menu) and a real doubles screenshot (Switch correctly disabled on slot 0's own TOP menu when its only party-mate is already active in the other field slot). **Bug 3 fix (idle-animation one-shot)**: `OpponentAnimTimer` in `battle_screen.tscn` gained `one_shot = true` (was unset, Godot's own default `false` = repeating) — the ONLY change needed; `_on_opponent_anim_timer_timeout()`'s own frame-alternation logic required no changes, since it's agnostic to how often the Timer fires. Confirmed zero dependents assumed continuous firing: the one existing test exercising this handler (`phase4d_doubles_visual_test.gd`'s `_test_anim_timer_doubles_independence`) calls `_on_opponent_anim_timer_timeout()` directly, bypassing the Timer node entirely, so it's unaffected either way. Deliberately NOT expanded into a real per-switch-in replay/reveal animation system, per this sub-phase's own explicit scope limit — the single bob now plays once near battle start and the sprite rests, rather than being re-triggered on each new Pokémon's own send-out. New `scenes/battle/m25b_menu_test.gd`/`.tscn`: 26/26, covering top-menu contents, Fight-menu contents/Back-button wiring, Switch's own disabled-without-a-valid-target state (both singles and implicitly doubles-shaped parties), Run's own wiring (deliberately NOT invoking it directly — matches `m23_6_battle_setup_test.gd`'s own established "never trigger a real `change_scene_to_file()` inside a headless/`--autoplay`-swept test" precedent), the fresh-turn-resets-to-TOP behavior, doubles per-slot independence, and the `OpponentAnimTimer.one_shot` property directly. Real, non-headless screenshot verification (8 screenshots, exceeding the required minimum): singles TOP/FIGHT/SWITCH/ITEM menus, doubles TOP/FIGHT menus (Switch correctly greyed out), and a 3-shot idle-animation rest sequence (A→B shows the one legitimate bob after `wait_time` elapses, B→C is pixel-identical — confirmed via a direct `ImageChops.difference` diff, not eyeballed — proving the sprite settles and does not continue alternating). A `--autoplay` leak-warning flake was checked specifically (given the Timer/scene changes) and confirmed pre-existing/RNG-dependent via an 8-run sample plus a git-stash A/B comparison against the M25a baseline, not newly introduced. - M25c (battle message/log authenticity — move-announcement text, target naming, damage/effectiveness reporting, pacing, turn separator): **COMPLETE** — 2026-07-19. Step 0 traced the existing log pipeline directly: `_wire_log_signals()` had zero move-announcement text at all — `_on_log_move_executed` was the ONLY thing that ever printed a "used MOVE!" line, and since `move_executed` fires once per TARGET (not once per action), a 2-target doubles spread hit would have printed the announcement TWICE, a genuine pre-existing authenticity gap this session's own Step 0 surfaced rather than assumed; `move_executed`'s own signal payload (`attacker, defender, move, damage`) carried no effectiveness/crit data at all, and `DamageCalculator.calculate()`'s own breakdown dictionary (`is_crit`, `effectiveness`) was computed but never threaded out of `BattleManager._do_damaging_hit` to any signal. Exact real-games phrasing/thresholds confirmed directly against `reference/pokeemerald_expansion/src/battle_message.c` rather than guessed: `STRINGID_CRITICALHIT` ("A critical hit!"), `STRINGID_SUPEREFFECTIVE` ("It's super effective!", effectiveness ≥ 2.0), `STRINGID_NOTVERYEFFECTIVE` ("It's not very effective…", 0 < effectiveness < 1.0), `STRINGID_ITDOESNTAFFECT` ("It doesn't affect {target}…", exactly 0.0 — the one effectiveness line that names a target in the real games too); a neutral 1.0× hit stays silent on effectiveness, matching source exactly. **New signals** (additive only, zero existing signal signatures changed, so none of the ~150 pre-existing `move_executed.emit(...)` call sites needed touching): `move_announced(attacker, defender, move)`, fired exactly ONCE per action from a single new choke point at the top of `_phase_move_execution` (right after `defender`/`move` are resolved, before any per-effect branch) — reachable only when the move genuinely IS being used, since every skip case (sleep/freeze/paralysis/confusion/flinch/recharge/loafing/Sky-Drop-held) is already filtered a phase earlier by `_phase_pre_move_checks`, which routes straight to `FAINT_CHECK` instead; `move_effectiveness_computed(defender, effectiveness, is_crit)`, fired from exactly the two REAL-hit branches inside `_do_damaging_hit` (a plain landed hit and a Substitute-absorbed hit), immediately before each one's own `move_executed` — deliberately NOT fired from the Wonder Guard/absorb-ability early returns, which already have their own dedicated `ability_triggered` message and would otherwise print a contradictory extra "no effect" line; `turn_started(turn_number)` plus a new public `turn_number: int` counter, incremented and emitted from `_phase_move_selection`'s own pre-existing fresh-entry guard (`_move_selection_active` false→true), the one place already structurally distinguishing "a new turn began" from "resuming a paused turn after human input." **UI rework**: `_on_log_move_executed` no longer prints the announcement at all (moved to a new `_on_log_move_announced`, the sole "used MOVE!" print site now, fixing the double-announcement-on-spread gap Step 0 found) — it now only reports the hit it was actually called for: a buffered crit/effectiveness line (via a new `_on_hit_effectiveness_computed` handler, safe by construction since `move_effectiveness_computed` always fires immediately before its corresponding `move_executed` in the same synchronous call, with zero risk of stale carryover since every `move_executed` handler consumes-and-clears the buffer immediately) followed by a target-named damage line. **Target naming**: the announcement names the target ("used MOVE on Y!") only when meaningful — omitted for a self-targeting move (`defender == attacker`, e.g. Swords Dance) and omitted for a REAL doubles spread hit (`move.is_spread and _is_doubles_mode`, not raw `move.is_spread` alone — a spread-flagged move used in an actual SINGLES battle only ever has one possible target and still gets named; this distinction was caught and deliberately tested before it could ship as a bug). Per-target damage lines always name their target unconditionally (both singles and doubles), a deliberate deviation from the real games (which never name a target in the base announcement line, relying on HP-bar-drain animation instead) — justified explicitly since this project's text-only log has no such animation to supply that context, and the user's own task framing asked for it. **Pacing**: implemented as a pure UI-layer paced-reveal QUEUE (`_queue_log_line`/`_run_log_reveal`, 0.6s between lines), deliberately NOT as an `await` inside `BattleManager.advance()` itself — the engine still resolves a whole turn synchronously/instantly exactly as before (zero changes to `battle_manager.gd`'s own resolution timing), only the UI staggers when each already-computed line becomes VISIBLE; relative order is unaffected (still a plain FIFO queue). Two bypass cases, both load-bearing: `--autoplay` (`_is_autoplay_run`, computed once in `_ready()` and reused by the pre-existing autoplay branch instead of re-deriving it) must never slow down, confirmed empirically — a direct `battle_screen.tscn --autoplay` timed run completed in 0.6s of TOTAL process time (Godot startup included), which would be impossible if per-line pacing were mistakenly active across a multi-turn battle; and `not is_inside_tree()` (this project's own established bare-`BattleScreen.new()` unit-test convention), needed because `get_tree()` itself prints a loud engine error when called outside the tree even though it still returns null gracefully — discovered when the new end-to-end signal-wiring test first surfaced it, fixed by checking `is_inside_tree()` directly instead of `get_tree() == null`. **Turn separator**: `──── Turn N ────`, a deliberately NOT-real-games-authentic choice (pokeemerald's own in-battle text log has no such line at all) justified as the simplest, clearest convention for a log that otherwise has no visual turn boundary. **Doubles compatibility**: confirmed via both a direct 2-target-different-effectiveness test and a real doubles screenshot — a single spread action now announces itself exactly ONCE ("Your A0 used Surf!") followed by two independently-thresholded per-target lines ("It's super effective! / Foe O0 took 32 damage!" then "It's not very effective… / Foe O1 took 9 damage!"). New `scenes/battle/m25c_message_log_test.gd`/`.tscn`: 17/17 — announcement foe-targeting/self-targeting/doubles-spread/spread-in-singles phrasing, all 4 effectiveness thresholds plus the neutral-silence and no-effect-suppresses-damage-line cases, crit-before-effectiveness ordering, a status-move-produces-nothing case, the turn separator, the 2-target spread scenario, and one genuine end-to-end test wiring a REAL `BattleManager.new()` (added to the test's own tree, mirroring `m25b_menu_test.gd`'s own established precedent for BattleManager specifically — unlike `BattleScreen`, it has no `@onready` scene-dependent children to crash on) through a real `bs._wire_log_signals()` call, proving the new signals actually fire from genuine gameplay rather than only that the handler logic is correct in isolation. Real, non-headless screenshot verification (4 screenshots): a real singles exchange (super-effective Water Gun named on its target, not-very-effective Ember back, turn separator, all rendered correctly in the live message box), a real doubles Surf spread hit (one announcement, two correctly-thresholded per-target lines), and a 2-shot pacing proof (t≈0: only the "Turn 1" separator visible despite the whole turn having already fully resolved internally; t≈2.5s: 4 more lines progressively revealed, `Turn 2` not yet — direct visual proof the staggered reveal genuinely works, not just internally consistent state). - Battle-dialogue signal-wiring recon (docs-only, not a milestone): **COMPLETE** — 2026-07-25. Programmatically cross-referenced all 133 `signal` declarations in `battle_manager.gd` against every `_bm.<signal>.connect(` call site in `battle_screen_shared.gd` (both the real in-battle message-box path, `_log()`/`_wire_log_signals()`, and the F3 debug panel, `_add_debug_entry()`/`_wire_debug_signals()`). **72 of 133 have no listener of either kind.** Confirmed the three player-suspected gaps directly: (1) `ability_triggered`/`ability_healed` are wired ONLY into `_wire_debug_signals()` (tagged `Ability & Immunity`, F3-only) — the readable per-effect-key text (`_ABILITY_TRIGGER_TEXT`, already built for the debug panel) never reaches `_log()`, so no ability activation of any kind (Intimidate, Levitate, Static, Speed Boost, weather-setters, etc.) produces any in-battle text during normal play. (2) `must_recharge` has no dedicated signal, but routes through the already-emitted `move_skipped(pokemon, reason)` signal (`reason="recharging"`) — which itself has ZERO listener anywhere, making this the single highest-leverage fix available: one connection would restore recharge AND 15 other reasons at once (`loafing`/`flinched`/`paralyzed`/`asleep`/`frozen`/`infatuated`/`confused`/`sky_drop_held`/`throat_chop`/`cant_use_twice`/`tormented`/`disabled`/`assault_vest`/`taunt`/`imprison`, all real, already-computed reason strings from `_phase_pre_move_checks`). (3) `charge_started` (two-turn-move first-turn text, e.g. "X flew up high!") fires correctly from both of its dispatch sites but has no listener at all. A narrower, partially-masked gap also found: `_on_log_secondary_applied`'s `match effect:` block (the function that DOES correctly narrate move-inflicted burn/freeze/paralysis/sleep/poison/toxic/confusion/flinch via `secondary_applied`) only recognizes those 8 `SE_*` cases and silently `return`s for anything else — meaning `SE_WRAP` (Bind/Wrap/Fire Spin/Clamp/etc.), `SE_PREVENT_ESCAPE`/`SE_TRAP_BOTH` (Mean Look/Block/Spider Web/Spirit Shackle/Jaw Lock), `SE_THROAT_CHOP`, and `SE_EERIE_SPELL` all fire the signal correctly but produce zero text. The remaining ~65 unwired signals were categorized, not individually scoped: move-mechanic volatile-infliction/outcome text (`protected`/`protect_broken`/`substitute_created`/`substitute_broke`/`disabled`/`encored`/`taunted`/`tormented`/`imprison_set`/`foresight_set`/`endured`/`destiny_bond_set`/`destiny_bond_triggered`/`move_called`/`move_effect_failed`/`pokemon_thawed`/`pokemon_transformed`/`type_changed`/`stat_changes_copied`/`pain_split_used`); meta-progression text with no in-battle equivalent at all (`exp_gained`/`level_up`/`ev_gained`/`money_awarded`/`move_learned`/`move_learn_skipped`); and a long tail of niche per-volatile signals (`curse_set`/`nightmare_set`/`ingrain_set`/`aqua_ring_set`/`magnet_rise_set`/`telekinesis_set`/`smack_down_set`/`tar_shot_set`/`sure_hit_set`/`laser_focus_set`/`octolock_set`/`leech_seeded`/`infatuated`/`rampage_lock_started`/`rampage_lock_ended`/`perish_song_activated`/`wrap_damage`/`wrap_ended`/`escape_prevented`/`stockpile_gained`/`stockpile_released`/`catch_attempted`/`forced_switch`). A handful of the 72 are legitimately non-narrative (`phase_changed`/`action_needed`/`replacement_needed` are internal state-machine signals, not player-facing text gaps) — flagged as such rather than silently included in the "needs text" count. - M26e-1 font recon (docs-only, not a milestone): **COMPLETE** — 2026-07-25. Reviewed both asset packs directly, per explicit instruction, before touching any code. **Emerald UI Pack contributes zero fonts** — confirmed no `Fonts/` directory and no `.ttf`/`.otf` files anywhere in the pack (`find` came up empty); it's purely a graphics reskin, expected to sit on top of Essentials' own fonts. **Essentials pack has 8 real, genuinely distinct TTF families** (`Fonts/*.ttf`, embedded family names confirmed via `PIL.ImageFont.getname()`, not just filenames): Power Clear Bold, Power Clear, Power Green Narrow, Power Green Small, Power Green, Power Red and Blue, Power Red and Blue Intl, Power Red and Green. Rendered all 8 at both a large reference size and the real small in-game sizes this project actually uses (13px/15px, health-box/menu text) for a direct legibility comparison. Found only **4 genuinely distinct shapes**: Clear Bold (boldest, most legible small) and Clear (clean regular) both held up best at 13px; Green Narrow is condensed/space-saving; Green Small was the WEAKEST at 13px despite its name suggesting the opposite — flagged explicitly so it isn't picked by name-assumption. The other 4 (Green/Red-and-Blue/Red-and-Blue-Intl/Red-and-Green) are visually shape-identical to each other — likely differing only in an intended per-message-color pairing in the real (uncompiled) Essentials engine, which this pulled asset pack can't confirm since it ships as a compiled RPG Maker XP distribution (`Game.exe` + binary `.rxdata`) with **zero Ruby source files** — no `Fonts.rb`-equivalent exists anywhere in it to check the real intended per-context mapping against. All 8 confirmed to have real glyph coverage for this project's own needed special characters (♂/♀, é). **A real scope-narrowing finding, mid-session, before any implementation**: `_font_menu` genuinely IS still on the old bitmap font and is a real open dynamic-load swap (`_load_battle_fonts()`), but `_font_healthbox` turned out to be a red herring — grep found ZERO usages of that GDScript variable anywhere in `battle_screen_shared.gd` beyond its own loading; the real font backing `NameLabel`/`LevelLabel`/`GenderLabel`/`HpNumberLabel` (confirmed directly in `health_group_panel_player.tscn`, all 4 sharing one `ext_resource`) is a **design-time reference baked directly into all 4 `health_group_panel*.tscn` files**, completely bypassing `_font_healthbox` at runtime. Migrating the health-box context for real means editing those 4 `.tscn` files' own font references, not the `_load_battle_fonts()` function — a materially different, larger-blast-radius change than the menu-button swap, correctly identified and held off before any edit was made, per explicit instruction. No code/test changes this session — recon and roadmap update only (M26e-1's own roadmap entry corrected in place with this finding).

- PokemonFactory/PokemonRegistry duplication consolidation (cleanup, not a milestone): **COMPLETE** — 2026-07-19. Follow-up to the finding flagged (not fixed) in M23.3's own CLAUDE.md bullet above. Direct comparison found the "nearly identical" characterization understated two real, confirmed bugs unique to M24b's `PokemonRegistry.get_species_resource()`/`BattlePokemon.from_trainer_mon()` pair, both absent from the older `PokemonFactory`: (1) no mono-type de-duplication — `pokemon.json` stores a mono-typed species as `[X, X]`, and `get_species_resource` copied it verbatim (a real, reachable Flying-Press/type-effectiveness-product bug for any mono-typed trainer Pokémon); (2) `from_trainer_mon` set `bp.evs` AFTER `from_species()` had already computed stats once, with no re-application — any `TrainerPartyMon` with nonzero EVs got a `BattlePokemon` whose stats silently didn't reflect them. Also confirmed missing `int()`-casts on most numeric fields (JSON float-coercion gotcha) and a missing `learnset` populate, both lower-impact. Caller audit: `PokemonFactory` has 4 real production callers (`team_storage.gd`, `random_team_generator.gd`, `movepool_resolver.gd`, `team_builder_screen.gd`) plus 4 test suites (`m23_3`/`m23_4`/`m23_5`/`m23_6`); `get_species_resource`/`from_trainer_mon` had zero real production callers — only `m24b_test.gd` — matching M24c's own already-documented "data ahead of consumer" pattern. Kept `PokemonFactory` canonical (more callers, more test coverage, more correct) and made `get_species_resource` a 1-line delegate to `PokemonFactory.build_species()`, fixing both the type-dedup and cast/learnset gaps for free. Did NOT delegate `from_trainer_mon` to `create_battle_pokemon()` — its ability-by-raw-ID and held-item-by-ID resolution has no equivalent in `create_battle_pokemon`'s slot-based ability API, and forcing a merge there was judged higher-risk than the value it'd add; instead added the missing `bp._calculate_stats()`/`bp.current_hp = bp.max_hp` pair directly, mirroring `PokemonFactory`'s own EV-then-recalculate pattern. Both bugs were confirmed untested by `m24b_test.gd`'s existing Section E (Makuhita's real `TrainerPartyMon` has 0 EVs; no assertion ever read `sp.types`' array shape), so zero existing expected values needed changing. Regression: `m24b_test.tscn` (the direct consumer) reran clean 61/61; two full sweeps matched the documented 156-file/23,310 baseline exactly except one difference — `m24c_test.tscn` flaked 27/28↔28/28 across repeat runs of the completely unmodified file (confirmed via 4 direct reruns, and confirmed it never calls `from_trainer_mon`/`get_species_resource` at all) — a newly-discovered, pre-existing, RNG-related flake unrelated to this session's changes, flagged here as a new addition to this file's own documented flaky-suite class rather than investigated further (out of this task's own scope). Nothing committed, per standing instruction.

## Development workflow

### Handoff: who does what

- **Rob commits.** Claude Code does not commit or push. Sessions end with
  changes left in the working tree; the standard closing line in this file's
  own status history is *"No commit made this session — per standing
  instruction, Rob commits."* (later sessions phrase it *"Nothing committed to
  git, per standing instruction."*). Both mean the same thing.
- **Rob runs full-suite sweeps.** Full `scripts/count_assertions.sh` sweeps
  are Rob's manual step. Claude Code runs tier-specific suites for the work in
  hand; it does not run a full sweep to populate a status column (see the
  `C/T/A` status key's own rules).
- **Rob owns approval.** The `A` slot in the `C/T/A` column is Rob's alone —
  never filled by Claude Code under any circumstances. See the status key.

### Running a verification scene

Self-contained, works from any cwd (see the working-directory rule above —
this form is mandatory, not stylistic):

```bash
/home/rob/Godot_v4.7.1-stable_linux.x86_64 --headless --path /home/rob/GodotAsImagined/as-imagined scenes/battle/SCENE.tscn
```

**Fresh-checkout baseline:** `scenes/overworld/m27a_step_resolver_test.tscn`
reads **44/44** (90 gated) in a clean clone, and **134/134** only after
`python3 scripts/gen_map_import.py all` regenerates the gitignored map JSONs
AND the corridor is baked — it announces which mode it is in. Both totals must
balance against `EXPECTED_TOTAL` via Z.99; a section that bails without
crediting `_gated` silently drops assertions the balance check then cannot
see, which is exactly how ~50 of them went missing once. Note `reference/pokeemerald_expansion` is a
git submodule, so a fresh clone needs `git submodule update --init` before any
generator runs. See docs/overworld_scope.md's "Regeneration chain" note.

**Verification scenes:**
- `scenes/battle/m36_leak_harness.tscn` — **[M36]** whole-roster LEAK / clean-run harness (784 tests): runs all 778 playable in-scope move scripts end to end and checks each TERMINATES, does not end in VM ERROR, leaves every battler at its resting position/scale/rotation/visibility/modulate/material, leaves no sprite or clone on the layer, and clears the scanline band. **This is defect detection, NOT fidelity verification** — it cannot tell you an animation looks right, only that it ran and cleaned up after itself. Its first run found **23 real leaks across 22 moves** (**all since FIXED at the root, 2026-08-03 — the baseline is EMPTY and must stay so**), one root cause in three dresses (the VM's cleanup nets only cover the TRACKED path, so direct `node.rotation`/`node.modulate`/`node.scale` writes and sprites never passed to `notify_spawned` all escape). Those are PINNED in `KNOWN_LEAKS` as a baseline that fails if the set changes in either direction; **shrinking it is the definition of done**, and the fix is a core-VM change deliberately left as its own task.
- `scenes/battle/m36d_batch_test.tscn` — **[M36D]** expansion batch (66 tests): asserts ported MOTION, not just that sprites appear — powder drifting downward from the TARGET while oscillating, vortex particles rising while circling, Bite's symmetric converge/retreat, the fist being genuinely static, the absorption orb travelling toward the ATTACKER (the one particle that runs backwards, so getting it wrong would look wrong in every draining move), an arc departing from its chord at mid-flight, the slice's 24-frame budget (20 motion + 4 hold), every mon task displacing AND exactly restoring position and scale, the elliptical orbit starting at the mon's own position, and end-to-end runs of the iconic moves this batch unblocked.
- `scenes/battle/m36e3_bg_behaviors_test.tscn` — **[M36E3]** BG-dependent behaviors (52 tests). Shaped around the two ways these fail INVISIBLY and PERMANENTLY: an open-ended effect registered as a COUNTED task hangs `waitforvisualfinish` forever (so the psychic cycle and the sliding scroll are asserted to NOT count, and to still be running after 200 frames), and a shake that resets the scroll to zero instead of its captured value silently cancels a scroll in progress (so the shake starts on an already-scrolled background and must return to exactly that). Also: the palette rotation's DIRECTION (rotating the wrong way makes the ramp flow backwards and the wave look like it is receding), the 8.8 accumulator delivering a pixel on the 4th frame for a quarter-pixel velocity (truncating instead would freeze every slow scroll dead), the mirror flag being CONDITIONAL on side, the haze blend table's source-exact plateaus, MetallicShine's recolour going through a SHADER not modulate (the defect this check caught) and its third sweep being real 32 frames, and — the headline — Surf installing the side-appropriate asset, travelling the MIRRORED direction per side, cycling 7 palette entries not the psychic 11, and ending on its own blend ramp with no sentinel.
- `scenes/battle/m36e_background_runtime_test.tscn` — **[M36E2]** background runtime (30 tests): BG integer-id -> name resolution through the extractor's own constant table, and above all the fade ORDER — the screen must be FULLY black at the moment the background swaps, asserted by recording the fade value at each swap, because a port that swapped first and faded second would look wrong in a way no 'did the texture change' check would catch. Also: the two wait opcodes releasing on different phases, changebg swapping with no fade at all, restorebg clearing only once black, an unknown background still costing its full frames (so pacing holds), and the leak invariant — finishing a run clears any background it swapped in.

will see it:

```bash

```

### Data pipeline scripts

Moves, abilities, and (as of the M18 item-data-infrastructure session) items each
follow the same two-track pattern: a hand-authored Python dict as the
human-editable source of truth, regenerated into Godot-native `.tres` Resource
files the engine loads at runtime. Run any of these from the project root, then
re-import (see the note above) before running a scene that depends on new/changed
`.tres` files:

```bash
python3 scripts/gen_moves.py      # data/moves/move_NNNN.tres    (MoveData)
python3 scripts/gen_abilities.py  # data/abilities/ability_NNNN.tres (AbilityData)
python3 scripts/gen_items.py      # data/items/item_NNNN.tres    (ItemData)
```

All three scripts share one structure: a list of dicts (`MOVES`/`ABILITIES`/`ITEMS`),
a `DEFAULTS` dict (skip a field in the emitted `.tres` when it equals its class
default, keeping files lean), a `FIELD_ORDER` list (explicit emit order), a
`render()` function, and a `main()` that writes one file per entry to a fixed
`data/<kind>/` directory, ID zero-padded to 4 digits.

Loading convention: `MoveRegistry.get_move(id)` / `ItemRegistry.get_item(id)` are
path-convention loaders (`res://data/<kind>/<kind>_%04d.tres % id`, no preload
table — see `move_registry.gd`'s own doc comment for the full rationale). There is
no `AbilityRegistry` — abilities are loaded ad hoc per call site (`load("res://data/abilities/ability_%04d.tres" % id) as AbilityData`)
because `AbilityManager`'s actual mechanic dispatch is 100% hardcoded ability-ID
constants and never reads `.tres` fields at battle runtime; the `.tres` layer there
is a metadata catalog (name/description/ai_rating/interaction flags), not a
mechanism input. **Items follow the `MoveRegistry` pattern** (`ItemRegistry`,
`scripts/battle/core/item_registry.gd`), since item mechanics are likewise
hardcoded in `ItemManager` (`HOLD_EFFECT_*` constants) but item data may need
by-ID lookup from future non-battle code (team-building, UI) the same way moves
do.

**Item scope note:** as of M18a, `gen_items.py`'s `ITEMS` dict only contains the
40 items M18a actually implemented — every future M18 sub-tier (M18b onward) must
add its items there and regenerate `.tres` files, matching the moves/abilities
convention, rather than wiring item data inline into `ItemManager` or a test file.
See `docs/decisions.md`'s item-data-infrastructure entry for the full rationale
and the M18a-era gap this closed.
